lens: LENS 1 — THEME REPRESENTATION: how to represent a market theme as a point-in-time object with an intensity time series, a membership set, and birth/death dates. Compares (a) LDA/topic-share attention, (b) embedding clusters, (c) LLM-labelled taxonomy, (d) keyword + confirmation gate.
bottom_line: Represent a theme as a versioned, append-only object whose DEFINITION (keyword sets + anchor embedding + seed membership) is FROZEN at birth and never re-fitted, with intensity = daily attention share innovation vs a trailing baseline. The published evidence supports the (d) keyword+confirmation-gate representation as the primary rail — it is the only family with a validated point-in-time construction (Caldara-Iacoviello GPR correlates 0.93 with a 7,000-article human-coded index) and the only one with 40 years of free archived history. LDA attention shares (a) are the strongest research-grade representation but their headline stock-market result is CONTEMPORANEOUS (25% R-squared, not a forecast) and their topic definitions are full-sample-fitted; (b) and (c) are unstable enough across re-runs that theme identity, not theme signal, becomes the dominant backtest risk. Critically, the literature says novelty/attention at birth predicts NEGATIVE aggregate returns and HIGHER volatility, so "theme is born -> go long the theme" is contradicted; the tradable claim must be cross-sectional (which beneficiaries), never directional timing of the theme itself.

key_findings.claim: (a) LDA/attention-share is the canonical representation and the mechanics are fully specified: K=180 topics selected by Bayes factor + 10-fold CV over K in {50..250}, Gibbs sampler 300 iterations, hyperparameters alpha=1, beta=1, no priors in the theta/phi estimates. Attention share at period tau is theta_hat(tau,k) = (sum over articles in tau of term-assignments to k) / (total term-assignments in tau) — i.e. a SHARE, which self-normalizes away secular growth in news volume. This is the exact intensity-series definition to copy.
key_findings.numbers: 763,887 WSJ articles 1984-01..2017-06; vocabulary 18,432 unigram+bigram terms; K=180 (170-180 optimal by Bayes factor AND 10-fold CV); 300 Gibbs iterations; alpha=beta=1; 23 first-level metatopics via hierarchical agglomerative clustering

key_findings.claim: The famous '25% of stock market returns' from LDA attention is CONTEMPORANEOUS EXPLANATION, not forecasting. The regression is monthly market return on AR(1) innovations in topic attention, 5 regressors chosen by lasso with post-selection inference. Only the macro (recession-attention -> output/employment) result is genuinely forward-looking. If pyfinagent copies this naively it reproduces exactly the call_transcript_gpr.py failure mode (contemporaneous, no forward predictability).
key_findings.numbers: Market returns: in-sample R2 0.25, out-of-sample R2 0.178 (expanding window, first half burn-in, annual re-fit). Recession coeff -0.35 (p=0.00), Problems -0.19 (p=0.00), Convertible/preferred -0.16 (p=0.21), Record high +0.12 (p=0.08), Options/VIX -0.11 (p=0.76). Benchmarks: CFNAI 4 sub-indices R2=0.02; 101 FRED-MD vars with 5-var lasso R2=0.09. Market volatility: in-sample R2 0.63, OOS 0.44. Forward-looking VAR: recession-attention shock (5th->95th pctile) -> industrial production -1.99% at 17 months, employment -0.92% at 20 months; ordered last -1.25%/-0.51%; EPU benchmark only -0.98%/-0.34%

key_findings.claim: Theme identity under LDA is stable at the METATOPIC level but churns violently at the topic level — and the churn is the theme lifecycle, not noise. BKMX explicitly classify topics as recurrent / seasonal / EMERGENT ('dormant for much of the sample, then triggered by particular events and often remain elevated after'). Their own examples of within-metatopic drift are exactly the operator's reference cases: 'technology' attention is flat but its contents go mainframes -> software -> mobile/internet; 'international affairs' shows episodic Russia spikes and the gradual emergence of China. This is direct evidence that a FIXED sector/metatopic bucket cannot express a theme, but a frozen sub-topic definition can.
key_findings.numbers: 180 topics -> 23 metatopics; metatopic attention share 'fairly stable over time' with 'a high degree of attention churn within metatopic clusters'; emergent-topic examples: terrorism {taliban, queda, suicide bomber, osama}, natural disasters {katrina, quake, tsunami, hurricane}

key_findings.claim: The only published result where news-theme attention beats standard factors OUT-OF-SAMPLE treats narratives as RISK FACTORS (covariance loadings), not as directional signals — and it defines the intensity innovation concretely as deviation from a 5-day moving average: z_tau = theta_tau - (1/5)*sum_{j=1..5} theta_{tau-j}. Copy that innovation definition. But note the topic model itself is imported wholesale from the full-sample BKMX estimation and the 180 topic LABELS are MANUALLY assigned by the authors — so the theme-definition layer carries full-sample look-ahead that the paper's OOS design does not correct.
key_findings.numbers: OOS MVE Sharpe 1.30 at K=5 (43.4 narratives selected on average) vs FFC6 benchmark 0.90 — ~50% improvement; unregularized (lambda=0, all 180 narratives) collapses to 0.79. Anomaly pricing errors 24% smaller than FFC6; mean |alpha| t-stat 2.9 (NF6) vs 3.4 (FFC6); 63% vs 74% significant pricing errors. OOS window 2001-01..2016-12; 1,850,401 stock-months, 15,831 stocks

key_findings.claim: (d) keyword + confirmation gate is the ONLY representation with a published human-validation number, and its design is a two-set proximity co-occurrence — exactly our defense_signal.py pattern generalized. GPR uses 8 categories, each a (topic_words) NEAR/2 (threat_words | act_words) query, plus an explicit EXCLUDED-words list derived from a false-positive audit (movies, sports, war anniversaries, obituaries). It is $0, deterministic, point-in-time by construction, has no fitting step to leak, and is already wired into pyfinagent.
key_findings.numbers: Correlation 0.93 (annual) between the automated GPR index and a human index built by reading and coding 7,000+ articles; 0.95 correlation between the 10-newspaper recent index and the 3-newspaper historical index; 0.88 between non-US and US newspapers' GPR; 0.86 with an independent narrative index; 0.82 with worldwide conflict deaths. Two-standard-deviation GPR shock -> fixed investment -1.5% at ~1yr, hours -0.6% at 1yr, GDP -0.3% over first year. Data free CC-BY 4.0 monthly + daily since 1985 (already fetched at backend/services/macro_regime.py:55)

key_findings.claim: BERTrend gives the complete, implementable birth/death state machine for a theme object, and its identity-continuity trick is the single most important design decision for backtest integrity: THE EMBEDDING OF THE FIRST OCCURRENCE OF A TOPIC IS RETAINED as the anchor, preventing drift. New clusters merge into an existing theme only if cosine similarity to the frozen anchor >= 0.7; otherwise a new theme_id is minted. Popularity accumulates when merged and decays exponentially when the theme is absent from a slice. State is assigned by percentile thresholds over a trailing retrospective window.
key_findings.numbers: merge threshold alpha=0.7 cosine (0.45 for user-seeded zero-shot topics); popularity p_t = p_{t-1} + |D_t| when merged, else p_t = p_{t-1} * exp(-lambda * dt^2) with lambda=0.01 and dt in days; classification: p < P10 -> noise, P10<=p<=P50 with positive slope -> weak signal, same band with negative slope -> noise (dying), p > P50 -> strong signal. Corpora: 367,248 arXiv abstracts (7-day slices), 184,811 NYT articles (2-day slices). NO quantitative precision/recall reported — authors state 'quantitative results about weak signal analysis are very challenging to obtain due to the lack of established metrics'

key_findings.claim: Theme BIRTH is detectable at $0 with a fully leak-free construction: n-gram entropy against a rolling training corpus that is deliberately OFFSET from the evaluation month. Glasserman-Mamaysky compute H_j(t) = -sum_i p_i(t) * log m_i(t) where p_i is the n-gram frequency in month t and m_i is the conditional probability estimated ONLY from months t-27..t-4 (a 24-month rolling window with a 3-month gap). The 3-month gap exists specifically so a phrase that first appeared last month is still scored as unusual — a direct analogue of what we need for detecting a theme in its first weeks. Unseen 4-grams get a floored probability of 0.25 via add-one smoothing (c(4gram)+1)/(c(3gram)+4).
key_findings.numbers: 367,331 Thomson Reuters articles on 50 large financial firms, 1996-01..2014-12, ~1,611 articles/month, 4-gram model, top 5,000 4-grams per month. ENTSENT_NEG raises cross-sectional R2 by an average of 0.22 over baseline, significant at lags up to 6 months; aggregate VAR impulse response of implied and realized volatility to ENTSENT_NEG is hump-shaped peaking at ~4 months. Results insensitive to 4,000 vs 5,000 n-gram cap and to the 0.25 floor

key_findings.claim: Shiller's SIR model is the canonical prior art for the theme lifecycle and it delivers one design-critical implication: a narrative epidemic 'will rise to a peak, and then fall and come to an end WITHOUT ANY CHANGE IN THE INFECTION OR REMOVAL RATES, and before everyone is infected.' Theme death is ENDOGENOUS. Therefore a death rule must be mechanical (attention rolls over) and must not wait for a contradicting external event. It also predicts the attention curve shape we should fit: bell-shaped, right-skewed.
key_findings.numbers: Kermack-McKendrick: dS/dt=-cSI, dI/dt=cSI-rI, dR/dt=rI. Epidemic size R_inf depends only on the ratio c/r; in the worked example (N=100, I0=1, c=.005, r=.05) 'going viral' (R_inf > N/2) requires c/r > .014. Scaling both c and r by a constant a rescales time only — so fast and slow epidemics are shape-identical, meaning the same detector works for weeks-to-months themes as for days

key_findings.claim: (b) embedding clusters: BERTopic's dynamic-topic mode achieves stable theme identity ONLY by fitting a global topic representation on the WHOLE corpus first and then computing per-timestep local c-TF-IDF against pre-calculated global IDF values. That is a look-ahead by construction and cannot be run point-in-time without re-architecting. The online (.partial_fit) path breaks it: HDBSCAN, the default clusterer, does not support incremental updating at all. BERTopic also assumes ONE topic per document, which is wrong for our case (an article about the AI buildout is simultaneously semis, power, and datacenter REITs).
key_findings.numbers: Topic coherence / diversity on 20NewsGroups: BERTopic-MPNET .166/.851 vs LDA .058/.749, NMF .089/.663, CTM .096/.886, Top2Vec .068/.718. BBC News: BERTopic .167/.792 vs LDA .014/.577. Trump tweets: BERTopic .066/.663 vs Top2Vec -.213/.698. c-TF-IDF: W(t,c) = tf(t,c) * log(1 + A/tf(t)); dynamic variant W(t,c,i) = tf(t,c,i) * log(1 + A/tf(t)) reusing the GLOBAL tf(t)

key_findings.claim: Run-to-run instability of unsupervised topic models is large enough to be the dominant backtest risk, and it is worse for BERTopic than the marketing suggests. Across 1,140 BERTopic runs the error size (documents dumped into the -1 no-topic bucket) had SD +/-4,604.76 on a mean of 56,281.51, and only 16% of 342 runs on the large corpus produced unique values; topic-NAME stability across runs showed no significant relationship to anything (Rho=-0.06, p=0.7137). Separately, LDA is 'internally consistent... however, these topics are not the true topics' — within-run stability is systematically better than between-run stability across Jensen-Shannon, Jaccard and Rank-Based-Overlap similarity measures.
key_findings.numbers: BERTopic: 1,140 runs, error size mean 56,281.51 (SD 4,604.76), Gini 0.46 (SD 0.10), keyword frequency 0.18 (SD 0.01), 16% unique values across 342 runs. LDA study: 50 simulated corpora x 50 LDA runs each with shuffling, K swept 7..13 against true K=10; 20 Newsgroups 18,000 docs, K swept 15..28 with the stability minimum correctly dipping at K=20

key_findings.claim: (c) LLM-labelled taxonomy produces the best semantic quality but its reproducibility profile is exactly wrong for a backtest: identical re-runs agree at purity 0.95 / ARI 0.92, but ANY perturbation of the input sample or prompt drops agreement to purity 0.67-0.70 / ARI 0.59-0.63. A theme taxonomy re-derived each cycle would silently re-partition ~1/3 of the corpus. It is also the only option with a recurring dollar cost and it degrades catastrophically on open models — Mistral-7B produced 1,418 topics where GPT-3.5 produced 151.
key_findings.numbers: Wiki (k=22): TopicGPT purity 0.74 / ARI 0.60 / NMI 0.70 vs LDA 0.64/0.52/0.67, BERTopic 0.58/0.28/0.50. Bills (k=24): 0.57/0.40/0.49 vs LDA 0.52/0.32/0.46, BERTopic 0.39/0.12/0.34. Human-judged misaligned topics: TopicGPT 30.3% vs LDA 62.4% (Wiki); 31.9% vs 80.2% (Bills). Stability vs default: identical runs 0.95/0.92/0.92; different generation sample 0.67/0.61/0.69; out-of-domain prompts 0.69/0.63/0.69; shuffled sample 0.70/0.63/0.70. Cost ~$100 per dataset run; topic merge uses Sentence-Transformer cosine >= 0.5; infrequent-topic removal thresholds 5 (Wiki) / 10 (Bills)

key_findings.claim: Any LLM-labelled theme taxonomy applied retroactively over a backtest window inside the model's training cutoff is contaminated, and prompt engineering does NOT fix it. The Lookahead-Propensity test is a cheap, portable gate we could actually run: query the model with ticker + date and NOTHING else, and read the first-token probability mass it puts on up/down instead of 'unknown'. LAP collapses to essentially zero immediately after the training cutoff, which is what makes it a usable contamination detector rather than a vibe.
key_findings.numbers: Llama-3.3-70B, cutoff December 2023. In-sample mean LAP peaks ~0.88 in 2020; post-cutoff 2024 max LAP across 7,806 firm-day queries is below 1e-4 with not a single firm-day above 0.5. Earnings-call: post-cutoff max LAP below 1e-5 across 6,619 firm-quarters. Detection regression: LLM signal 0.141% next-day return (t=7.55), LLM x LAP interaction +0.162% (t=3.64); at LAP=1.0 the marginal effect is 0.303%, more than double. Validation: recall-query signal alone predicts returns, theta=0.264 (t=3.53) pooled, 0.306 (t=3.59) high-LAP, -0.159 (t=-0.33, statistically zero) low-LAP. Authors: 'common mitigation strategies such as prompt engineering or identifier masking are ineffective'

key_findings.claim: Point-in-time language models are the only clean way to use modern embeddings for a theme representation over historical data, and they now exist as open weights on HuggingFace — but they are a GPU artifact, not a $0 local artifact. The chronological discipline is the part we can copy for free: 'for each calendar year t, we use the PIT model available at the end of the previous year' to embed that year's articles. Encouragingly, the strict-PIT models perform close to their full-sample (leaking) counterparts, so enforcing point-in-time discipline does NOT destroy the economic signal.
key_findings.numbers: PIT-1.5B (1.5B params, 170B tokens) and PIT-4B (4.2B params, 1T tokens); embedding dim 4,096, seq len 2,048, vocab 50,304; ~28,000 GPU-hours. OOS annualized Sharpe from penalized Max-Sharpe-Ratio regression on news embeddings: PIT-4B ~1.0-1.5 vs ChronoGPT baseline ~0.7. HellaSwag 72.2% vs Gemma-3-4B 76%; PIQA 78.9% vs 80%; WinoGrande 64.2% vs 69.5% — gap narrowed but not closed. Evaluated on a single benchmark dataset

key_findings.claim: MEASURED IN-REPO: sklearn 1.8.0, sentence_transformers 5.5.1, torch 2.12.0 and transformers 5.11.0 are already installed in the venv; gensim, umap, hdbscan and bertopic are NOT. So option (a) via sklearn LatentDirichletAllocation and a frozen-anchor embedding scheme via sentence_transformers are buildable today at zero new dependencies, while BERTopic requires 3 new deps including a C-extension clusterer that cannot do incremental updates anyway.
key_findings.numbers: OK sklearn 1.8.0; OK sentence_transformers 5.5.1; OK torch 2.12.0; OK transformers 5.11.0; OK numpy 2.4.4; OK scipy 1.17.1. MISS gensim, umap, hdbscan, bertopic. backtest_engine.py:50 _NUMERIC_FEATURES has exactly 37 entries, zero news- or theme-derived

key_findings.claim: MEASURED LIVE 2026-08-04: the Alpha Vantage NEWS_SENTIMENT payload already carries a per-article `topics` array with per-topic relevance_score AND a `ticker_sentiment` array giving per-ticker relevance_score + sentiment_score on the SAME article. That second array is a ready-made, timestamped, cross-sector co-mention graph — one AVGO article tagged AVGO 1.000, MU 0.623, NVDA 0.613, AMD 0.603, PLTR 0.560. It is the cheapest available seed for a theme membership set. CAVEAT I could not close today: the full `topics` taxonomy is unverified — I observed only 3 values in-sample (earnings, financial_markets, finance) and the free REST key hit its 25-requests/day cap before I could enumerate it, while the documentation page truncated before the NEWS_SENTIMENT section.
key_findings.numbers: Observed article time_published 20260804T075307; topics observed: earnings (relevance 0.918609, 0.940316), financial_markets (0.813946), finance (0.729909). ticker_sentiment relevance/sentiment pairs: AVGO 1.000000/0.301412, MU 0.623355/0.120358, NVDA 0.613456/0.137582, AMD 0.603127/0.119565, PLTR 0.559974/0.052670. Free-tier REST cap measured at 25 requests/day (hit); MCP connector rail still served data

key_findings.claim: TDT (the 1998 DARPA program) is the year-less canonical prior art and it already fixed the vocabulary we should adopt: an EVENT is a specified occurrence with particular actors, locations and timeframe; a TOPIC is 'a seminal event plus all related events and background information'. That is exactly the operator's four reference cases — Ukraine invasion (event) vs the defense rearmament theme (topic). TDT also defines First Story Detection as its own task with its own miss-rate / false-alarm-rate / detection-cost evaluation, and used a vector-space model with a dissimilarity threshold plus a TIME-DECAY function down-weighting older stories.
key_findings.numbers: Five TDT tasks: Topic Tracking, Link Detection, Topic Detection, First Story Detection, Story Segmentation. Evaluation metrics: miss rate, false alarm rate, weighted detection cost. Exact numeric results were not extractable from the fetched pilot report; the stated core difficulty is 'distinguishing genuinely new events from event continuations' and the sensitivity/specificity tradeoff in threshold selection

negative_or_null_results: THE BIG ONE — buying a theme at peak attention is a documented loss-maker. Specialized/thematic ETFs deliver -6% per year risk-adjusted over their first five years (FFC-4 alpha -0.50%/month), losing ~30% risk-adjusted over 5 years, and the underperformance is NOT explained by fees or hedging demand — it is driven by overvaluation of the underlying stocks at launch. Split by pre-launch characteristics: specialized ETFs whose holdings had the HIGHEST pre-launch returns and MEDIA SENTIMENT delivered -0.53%/month, versus -0.20%/month for those launched after low pre-launch returns/sentiment. After year 5 the underperformance is statistically indistinguishable from zero. Appendix Table F.6 shows a pure stock-level version — long the top-5 holdings of ETFs launched in the previous 12 months — produces 'a similar magnitude of underperformance'. Direct implication: our entry rule must fire at the WEAK-signal stage (BERTrend P10-P50 band with positive slope), and any theme already in the STRONG band with elevated media sentiment should be a fade or an exclusion, not a buy. https://www.nber.org/system/files/working_papers/w28369/w28369.pdf

News NOVELTY predicts NEGATIVE aggregate returns, not positive. An increase in news entropy forecasts a -2.821% year-ahead market return per one standard deviation (-2.7% in the pre-COVID subsample), with positive out-of-sample R2 across horizons (0.024 at h=15 months to 0.051 at h=21 months; the ENT_NEWS component reaches 0.060-0.096). Meanwhile EPU, sentiment, CAPE, VIX, CAY and 60-month-lagged Fama-French factors all produce 'overwhelmingly negative' out-of-sample R2. Entropy exposure carries a NEGATIVE cross-sectional risk premium of -0.060% to -0.091% per month. So 'a new theme is being born' is, at the aggregate level, a bearish macro signal — the money is in cross-sectional selection among beneficiaries, not in timing the market off theme births. Corpus: 1,642,517 Thomson Reuters articles on S&P 500 firms 1996-01..2022-12; LSTM with 177,488 parameters, 100-dim GloVe, hidden dim 16, rolling 6-month retraining, ENT defined as month t minus month t-12. https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2309.05560

Glasserman-Mamaysky's own long-short portfolio tests on their entropy-sentiment signal are weak and they say so: 'our tests have low power as the only significant alpha is from the interacted negative-positive sentiment sort.' Sharpe ratios across the fraction x holding-period grid run 0.124 to 0.4665 for the negative-sentiment sort and are frequently NEGATIVE for the positive-vs-negative sort (e.g. -0.2769, -0.246, -0.20735, -0.1393). The robust result is VOLATILITY forecasting, not return forecasting — the same asymmetry as our own call_transcript_gpr.py finding. A theme-intensity feature should therefore be pre-registered as a risk/regime input first and only promoted to an alpha input if it independently clears the gate.

Naive embedding-clustering of news headlines into topic dummies produces a statistically insignificant model. K-means with K=5 (silhouette-selected) over all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings of 26,750 AAPL headlines 2016-2024, regressed on next-day returns: R2 = 0.035, overall F-statistic p = 0.142 (insignificant), only Topic_0 (-0.0058, p=0.036) and Topic_4 (+0.0045, p=0.037) individually significant, NO out-of-sample test, no hold-out, no cross-validation, and the authors concede 'difficulty in interpreting the resulting topics'. The paper also provides no mechanism at all for maintaining cluster identity across time periods. This is the failure mode of doing (b) casually. https://arxiv.org/html/2510.06864v1

BERTrend reports NO quantitative precision/recall/F1 for its weak-signal detector and states plainly that 'relying on temporal popularity fluctuations alone isn't ideal, as both weak and noise signals behave very similarly', that there is no ground truth and no accepted benchmark, and that performance is sensitive to BERTopic params, merge threshold, granularity and retrospective period. Its thresholds (P10/P50) are 'empirically fixed'. So the state machine is a good SHAPE to copy but its parameters carry zero external validation and must be treated as free parameters entering our PBO count.

Look-ahead bias is systematically unacknowledged in the LLM-finance literature we would be borrowing from: across 164 main-conference papers 2023-2025, look-ahead bias is acknowledged in only 26.8% and survivorship bias in 1.2%; no single bias appears in more than 28% of papers. The authors' conclusion — 'many published numbers do not support the claims that readers and practitioners want to make from them' — applies directly to any 2024+ LLM-theme-labelling result we might cite as precedent. https://arxiv.org/html/2602.14233v1

LDA is internally consistent but NOT recovering true topics: in a controlled simulation with known K=10, within-run stability is systematically better than between-run stability across Jensen-Shannon, Jaccard and Rank-Based-Overlap, i.e. re-running the same model on the same data yields a different partition. Any backtest whose theme definitions are re-fit per window is therefore comparing different objects across windows.

Coverage gap for the operator's reference cases: nothing free reconstructs a point-in-time article-level COVID->pharma theme. The Alpha Vantage news archive starts 2022-02-24, which post-dates COVID entirely and coincides almost exactly with the Ukraine invasion, so case 1 is unbuildable from AV and case 3 sits on the archive boundary. GPR (daily, free, since 1985) covers cases 3 and 4 but is a single geopolitical theme, not a general registry. Any claim that we can backtest all four reference cases on free data is false as of today.

The two strongest research representations both carry an uncorrected look-ahead in the theme-DEFINITION step even though their downstream evaluations are honest: BKMX's 180-topic LDA is 'based on a single estimation using the full data sample' with hand-assigned labels, and Narrative Asset Pricing imports that same full-sample model. Their OOS numbers (0.178 return R2; 1.30 Sharpe) are OOS with respect to coefficients, not with respect to what the themes ARE. We cannot cite those numbers as evidence that a re-derived-each-cycle theme set would work.
recommendation_for_pyfinagent:
PRIMARY: build a versioned, append-only `theme_registry` + `theme_intensity` pair in BigQuery, with a HYBRID (d)-primary / (a)-secondary representation. Concretely:

1) THEME OBJECT (frozen-at-birth, never re-fit). Fields: theme_id (immutable), definition_version, birth_date, death_date (nullable), status in {candidate, weak, strong, dying, dead}, keyword_spec {topic_words[], confirm_words[], excluded_words[], proximity_n}, anchor_embedding (sentence_transformers, computed ONCE from the first-window article set and never recomputed — BERTrend's exact anti-drift rule), seed_members[] (tickers), provenance (who/what minted it). Any change to keyword_spec or anchor mints a NEW theme_id with a `supersedes` pointer; the old series is never rewritten. This is the single design decision that makes the backtest auditable, and it is a direct answer to the 'relabeling breaks a backtest' question — you never relabel, you version.

2) INTENSITY. Daily attention SHARE (Bybee eq. 4: theme term/article mass over TOTAL mass that day — self-normalizing, so news-volume growth cannot masquerade as theme growth), plus the innovation z_tau = theta_tau - mean(theta_{tau-1..tau-5}) from Narrative Asset Pricing. Persist BOTH level and innovation. Store popularity with BERTrend decay p_t = p_{t-1}*exp(-0.01*dt^2) so a theme that stops being written about dies on a clock rather than on our opinion.

3) BIRTH GATE = novelty AND confirmation, mirroring defense_signal.py's AND-gate rationale. Novelty leg: Glasserman-Mamaysky 4-gram entropy with the OFFSET rolling window (train on t-27..t-4 months, evaluate month t, add-one smoothing floor 0.25) — this is $0, pure-Python, and leak-free by construction. Confirmation leg: a price/flow confirmation exactly as defense_signal.py does (GPR-Acts AND XAR 5-day momentum > 0). Fire birth only when BOTH fire, and record the firing evidence in the theme row.

4) DEATH RULE = mechanical, per Shiller: attention peaks and rolls over endogenously, so do NOT wait for a contradicting event. Use BERTrend's percentile state machine over a trailing window (p < P10 -> dead; P10<=p<=P50 with negative slope -> dying). Additionally hard-code the Ben-David finding as an ENTRY EXCLUSION, not just an exit: a theme whose members already show top-quartile trailing returns AND top-quartile media sentiment is in the -0.53%/month regime and must be excluded from new BUYs regardless of intensity.

5) DISCOVERY CHANNEL (secondary, (a)). Run sklearn LatentDirichletAllocation (already installed, zero new deps) on the persisted corpus with SMALL K on an expanding window, purely to PROPOSE candidate themes. A proposal never becomes a live theme automatically — it goes to a promotion step where an LLM writes the keyword_spec and seed_members ONCE, the operator approves, and the definition is then frozen. This gets LDA's discovery benefit with none of its re-fit instability, and confines LLM usage to one cycle-level call per theme birth (not per ticker, not per cycle).

6) FIRST BUILDABLE ARTIFACT, given the measured gaps. The news corpus is not persisted at all (bq_writer targets news_articles / news_sentiment which do not exist and it fails open), so there is no history to compute any of this over. Step one is therefore: create those two tables, start persisting Alpha Vantage NEWS_SENTIMENT with its `topics` and `ticker_sentiment` arrays verbatim plus an ingest_timestamp, and backfill to 2022-02-24. Until that exists, every theme representation is un-backtestable and therefore un-gate-able. In parallel, seed the registry with the ONE theme that already has 40 years of free archived intensity — geopolitics via GPR/GPRD, already fetched at backend/services/macro_regime.py:55 — because it is the only theme that can produce a DSR/PBO-eligible sample today.

7) GATE FRAMING. Pre-register theme_intensity as a RISK/REGIME feature first, not an alpha feature. The evidence is lopsided: novelty and attention forecast VOLATILITY robustly (OOS R2 0.44 in BKMX; hump-shaped 4-month IRF in Glasserman-Mamaysky) and forecast RETURNS weakly and often with the wrong sign (-2.8%/yr for novelty; SR 0.12-0.47 with negative cells for the long-short sorts). Add exactly two columns to backtest_engine.py::_NUMERIC_FEATURES (theme_intensity_z, theme_age_days) and make the promotion claim cross-sectional (does theme membership improve the RANKING of candidates) rather than directional. Every free parameter in the state machine (0.7 merge, lambda=0.01, P10/P50, 5-day innovation window, 24-month/3-month entropy offset) must be counted in the PBO trial count — that is 6+ knobs before any signal exists.
rejected_options: BERTopic as the LIVE theme representation — REJECTED on three independent grounds: (i) its dynamic-topic mode only achieves stable identity by fitting global topics over the whole corpus and reusing pre-calculated GLOBAL IDF values per timestep, which is look-ahead by construction; (ii) the online .partial_fit path cannot use HDBSCAN, its default and best clusterer, so going point-in-time means changing the algorithm; (iii) measured run-to-run instability is severe (only 16% unique values across 342 runs; topic-name stability Rho=-0.06, p=0.7137). It also needs 3 new deps (umap, hdbscan, bertopic) that are not installed. Keep sentence_transformers embeddings, drop the BERTopic pipeline.

Per-cycle LLM theme labelling ('ask the model what theme this article is about', option (c) as a live rail) — REJECTED. Perturbing the sample or the prompt drops TopicGPT's agreement with its own default run to purity 0.67-0.70 / ARI 0.59-0.63, meaning ~1/3 of the corpus gets re-partitioned on any input change, which silently rewrites history in a backtest. It is also the only option with a recurring metered cost (~$100/dataset-run in the paper), violating the $0 constraint, and it degrades catastrophically on the local/open models we could afford (Mistral-7B generated 1,418 topics vs GPT-3.5's 151). LLM labelling is retained ONLY as a one-shot naming/membership step at theme birth, where its 30.3% vs LDA's 62.4% human-judged misalignment rate is a real advantage and its output is immediately frozen.

Re-estimating an LDA topic model on an expanding window each cycle and matching topics across vintages — REJECTED as the primary rail. Even with the same data, LDA's between-run partition differs from its within-run partition across all three standard similarity measures, so cross-vintage topic matching is a research project in itself, not a feature. BKMX and Narrative Asset Pricing both dodge this by estimating ONCE on the full sample and hand-labelling, which we cannot copy without importing their look-ahead. LDA stays as a proposal generator whose output is frozen on promotion.

Copying the BKMX '25% of stock market returns' framing as the justification for a theme alpha — REJECTED. That number is contemporaneous explanation with OOS R2 0.178, not a forecast, and it is the same statistical shape that already caused call_transcript_gpr.py to be scoped down to a risk filter. Repeating it would repeat the documented failure mode the operator explicitly asked us not to repeat.

Adopting the Alpha Vantage `topics` field as THE theme taxonomy — REJECTED as primary. The observed values (earnings, financial_markets, finance) are sector/event categories, not themes in the operator's sense; nothing in that taxonomy can express 'AI datacenter buildout propagating to memory' or 'European rearmament'. It is worth persisting verbatim as a free covariate and as a coarse routing key, but it cannot carry the cross-sector hop the four reference cases require. (Full taxonomy remains unverified — see open questions.)

Point-in-time LLMs (ChronoBERT / ChronoGPT / PIT-4B) as the embedding backbone — REJECTED for now on the local-machine constraint. PIT-4B is 4.2B params trained with ~28,000 GPU-hours; the operator's machine already sits at 13.7/16GB and the existing local-LLM verdict rejected pipeline localization on exactly this basis. The transferable part is free: adopt their chronological rule ('for each calendar year t, use the model available at the end of the previous year') for whichever encoder we do use, and freeze the encoder version per theme_id.

A pure sector/GICS bucket as the theme container — REJECTED with direct evidence. BKMX show metatopic-level attention is flat while its CONTENTS churn completely (technology: mainframes -> software -> mobile/internet), which is precisely why peer_leadlag_screen.py's GICS-sector grouping cannot express a cross-sector hop. The theme object must be its own entity with its own membership set, not a re-labelling of an existing sector partition.
open_questions: UNRESOLVED MEASUREMENT: the full Alpha Vantage NEWS_SENTIMENT `topics` taxonomy. I observed only 3 values live (earnings, financial_markets, finance); the free REST key returned 'standard API rate limit is 25 requests per day' before I could enumerate a broad sample, and the documentation page truncated before the NEWS_SENTIMENT section. Someone must re-run a 1000-article pull on a fresh day and record the distinct topic set + whether `topics` is queryable as a filter parameter. Do not assume the ~15-topic list circulating in third-party write-ups.

Corpus-scale feasibility of option (a) on OUR data. BKMX needed 763,887 full-text articles and an 18,432-term vocabulary to support K=180. Alpha Vantage returns headlines + short summaries, not full text, at roughly tens-to-hundreds of articles per day. What is the largest K that is actually estimable on a summaries-only corpus of that size, and does a small-K LDA (say K=15-30) produce anything more useful than the AV `topics` field we get for free? This should be settled empirically before any LDA code ships.

How many independent themes can we support before PBO kills us? Every theme is a hypothesis and every knob (0.7 merge threshold, lambda=0.01 decay, P10/P50 bands, 5-day innovation window, 24-month/3-month entropy offset, proximity N) is a trial. With PBO <= 0.5 as an immutable gate and only ~4.4 years of AV history, the effective degrees of freedom may already be exhausted by the state machine before a single theme is tested. Needs an explicit trial-count budget written into the contract BEFORE building.

Is theme BIRTH even the right entry point given the ETF evidence? Ben-David et al. show the loss comes from entering after attention peaks, and Glasserman/Mamaysky/Qin show novelty itself is bearish at the aggregate. It is possible the only profitable entry is DURING the weak-signal band and the only profitable use of the strong-signal band is as an EXIT or a short-side exclusion. This asymmetry should be pre-registered as a hypothesis with separate criteria for each band, not discovered post hoc.

Where does the intensity series come from for themes with no dedicated free index? GPR gives us geopolitics back to 1985 and EPU gives policy uncertainty, but there is no free Caldara-Iacoviello equivalent for 'AI datacenter buildout' or 'GLP-1'. Do we accept a 2022-02-24 start (AV archive) for all non-geopolitical themes, and if so does a ~4.4-year sample ever clear DSR >= 0.95?

Does the anchor-freeze rule survive a genuine theme MUTATION? Shiller explicitly notes narratives 'mutate and get contagious again'. Under the frozen-anchor design a mutated theme (AI-training-compute -> AI-inference-power) mints a NEW theme_id and loses its history. Is that correct (clean, auditable, but sample-destroying) or should there be an explicit lineage-aware aggregation for backtesting? No source I read resolves this — BERTrend simply keeps the first embedding forever and does not discuss mutation.

Can the Lookahead-Propensity test actually be run on our rail? It requires first-token logprobs at the answer position. The Anthropic API does not expose token logprobs the way the paper's Llama-3.3-70B setup does, so if we ever use an LLM for retroactive theme labelling in a backtest we may have NO way to run the contamination diagnostic the literature says is necessary. This is an argument for keeping LLM involvement strictly forward-only (label at birth, never retroactively).

TDT's First-Story-Detection numeric baselines (miss rate / false alarm rate / detection cost) were not extractable from the fetched pilot report. If we build a birth detector we have no external benchmark for what a reasonable false-alarm rate looks like on news streams. Worth one more pass at the NIST TDT evaluation overview papers before setting our own thresholds.

lens: LENS 2 — Beneficiary mapping (theme -> second-order beneficiaries) without paid supply-chain data (FactSet SPLC / Bloomberg SPLC / Compustat Segments)
bottom_line: There is no free substitute for a firm-level customer-supplier database, and the one anomaly that would have justified building one (Cohen-Frazzini customer momentum) is measurably dead in the exact slice pyfinagent trades: value-weighted post-2005 alpha 0.62%/mo t=1.54 (insignificant), only ~232 US firms/month have an identifiable public customer link at an average $1.5B market cap, and the effect is fully subsumed by analyst-co-coverage momentum (4-factor alpha falls 0.97 t=2.47 -> 0.43 t=1.09). The one free route that is both ticker-keyed and empirically the strongest surviving cross-firm link is the NEWS CO-MENTION graph — the only cross-firm momentum variant that survived transaction costs in the only paper that tested all of them side-by-side (1.29%/mo t=3.56 net of 16bps vs "insignificant alphas" for every other link type) — and pyfinagent can build it at $0 from the Alpha Vantage NEWS_SENTIMENT archive it already has a key for.

key_findings.claim: Cohen & Frazzini (2008) original magnitude and, critically, its COVERAGE: the link data covers only 12.8% of CRSP names equal-weighted / 9.2% value-weighted, customers sit at the 91st size percentile, and 78% of links are cross-industry (which is the good news for a cross-sector hop).
key_findings.numbers: VW 3-factor alpha 1.555%/mo [t=3.60]; VW 4-factor 1.376% [t=3.13]; VW 5-factor (adds Pastor-Stambaugh liquidity) 1.237% [t=2.99]; EW 3-factor 1.306% [t=4.67]. Sample 1981-2004. 30,622 firm-year relationships / 11,484 unique supplier-customer pairs 1980-2004. Firms/yr 390-1470 (mean 918). Firm coverage of CRSP: 12.8% EW, 9.2% VW. Mean customer = 19.80% of supplier sales (median 14.68%). Mean link duration 2.7 years. 78% of links cross-industry. Drift: large firms close 69% of the gap in month 1 and the remaining 31% over the next 6 months; small firms 35% then 65% over 6 months. Suppliers' own 3-factor alpha is -41bps/mo (the universe itself underperforms).

key_findings.claim: POST-PUBLICATION DECAY IS REAL AND LARGE for customer momentum. Pinchuk (2023) replicates Cohen-Frazzini and then splits at the 2005 discovery date: the value-weighted version — the one relevant to a 500-1000 large/mid-cap universe — loses statistical significance entirely.
key_findings.numbers: EW long-short 1.52%/mo [t=4.74] in 1978-2004 -> 0.62%/mo [t=2.12] in 2005-2018. VW 1.30% [t=3.03] -> 0.62% [t=1.54] INSIGNIFICANT. FF5+UMD EW alpha 1.37% [t=3.96] -> 0.59% [t=1.89] insignificant at 5%. Decay ~59% EW / ~52% VW. Sample 255,747 firm-month links, 4,746 public firms 1977-2018 (merged: 145,489 firm-months, 3,266 firms). Author states 'customer momentum is stronger across small stocks'. Consistent with McLean-Pontiff's ~50% average post-publication decay.

key_findings.claim: Ali & Hirshleifer (JFE 2020) is the decisive negative result for the customer-supplier channel: customer momentum is SUBSUMED by shared-analyst-coverage momentum, and only 232 US firms per month even have a usable public-customer link (average market cap $1.5B, i.e. below pyfinagent's universe floor). Their customer-momentum factor sample ENDS June 2006 for data-availability reasons.
key_findings.numbers: CF (connected-firm, shared analyst) momentum: 1.68%/mo alpha [t=9.67], information ratio 1.71 over 1984-2015. Customer momentum factor alone: mean 1.15 [t=3.44], 4-factor alpha 0.97 [t=2.47], 5-factor alpha 1.29 [t=3.62]. AFTER adding CF momentum: 4-factor+CF alpha 0.43 [t=1.09] INSIGNIFICANT; 5-factor+CF alpha 0.74 [t=1.79] insignificant at 5%. Industry momentum -0.24 [t=-2.06], geographic -0.23 [t=-2.46], supplier-industry -0.26 [t=-1.73], customer-industry -0.42 [t=-2.86], technology -0.52 [t=-2.90] — all insignificant or NEGATIVE after CF control. Avg # focal firms/month: CF 3,010 (avg size $3,292M) vs Customer momentum 232 (avg size $1,546M).

key_findings.claim: (a) HOBERG-PHILLIPS TNIC IS THE WRONG TOOL FOR BENEFICIARY MAPPING — verified in their own readme. TNIC is explicitly PURGED of vertical relationships. It gives you COMPETITORS, not beneficiaries. Anyone proposing TNIC for a theme->supplier hop has mis-read the data.
key_findings.numbers: Readme verbatim: 'Note: TNIC industries are also purged for vertical relationships from the input/output tables'. Calibration: 'the likelihood of two randomly drawn firms being deemed related in their TNIC-3 is also 2.05%' (matched to 3-digit SIC coarseness). Built from Item 101 Reg S-K product descriptions in 10-Ks, 1996-present, cosine similarity in [0,1], symmetric square matrix incl. self-pairs. MEASURED 2026-08-04: tnic3_data.zip HTTP 200 no auth, content-length 151,403,342 bytes, last-modified 2024-11-20, 2 zip entries, tnic3_data.txt uncompressed 679,225,418 bytes. Coverage claim conflicts across HP pages: industryclass.htm says 1989-2021, the library index says 1989-2023.

key_findings.claim: (a-corrected) The RIGHT free Hoberg-Phillips asset is VERTICAL TNIC (VTNIC, Fresard-Hoberg-Phillips): a DIRECTED firm-pair upstream/downstream relatedness score built by matching 10-K product vocabulary to BEA Input-Output commodity vocabularies. It is free, no registration. But it measures POTENTIAL vertical relatedness, not observed trade, and has NEVER been validated for return prediction.
key_findings.numbers: Free, HTTP 200 no auth (measured 2026-08-04): VertNetwork_10gran.zip 854,396,826 bytes last-mod 2024-11-04; VertNetwork_all.zip 8,299,438,257 bytes last-mod 2026-06-05; VertInteg.zip 1,515,007 bytes. Schema: gvkey1, gvkey2, vertscore, year — asymmetric/directed. '10% granularity' = top 10% of ALL pairwise scores that year, i.e. 10% of random firm pairs are flagged 'related' (vs NAICS-based comparators calibrated at 1.37% and 9.48%). Validation reported: text-based network is 'roughly four times stronger in predicting these direct 10-K statements [of vertical integration] than is the NAICS-based network' (Table IA.III.1) and also beats NAICS on US Census related-party trade (Table IA.III.2). Paper sample ~7,000 firms 1996-2008. BEA base: 424 commodities / 426 industries in the 2002 Make table, sub-commodity descriptions averaging 8 words. NO precision/recall vs actual customer-supplier pairs and NO asset-pricing test anywhere in the paper.

key_findings.claim: HARD BLOCKER on both TNIC and VTNIC for a $0 shop: the files are keyed on gvkey ONLY — no CIK, no ticker, no permno. gvkey is a Compustat identifier and the crosswalk is a WRDS product. Free workarounds exist but are themselves approximations.
key_findings.numbers: Both readmes confirm exactly three data columns plus year: 'Each file contains a gvkey1 and a gvkey2 variable in addition to the score variable.' HP note they used a WRDS-supplied expanded historical CIK->gvkey mapping 'as the base CIK variable in COMPUSTAT only contains current links'. Free crosswalk candidates found: the R `farr` package gvkey_ciks table (78,339 rows, 5 variables) and github.com/leoliu0/cik-cusip-mapping (CIK<->CUSIP derived from EDGAR 13D/13G). SEC company_tickers.json gives CIK<->ticker free.

key_findings.claim: (b) NEWS CO-MENTION GRAPHS: Schwenkler & Zheng recover only about ONE THIRD of the Compustat-Segments customer-supplier links they are compared against, and lose two-thirds of firms to entity resolution. Their paper delivers AGGREGATE risk prediction, not cross-sectional stock alpha — do not cite it as an alpha result.
key_findings.numbers: Reuters full text 2006-10-20 to 2013-11-20, 106,521 articles, avg article ~600 words / 21 sentences. Network spans 'over 6,000 firms and 16,000 business links'; 308,512 link instances; 2.90 firm connections per article. Verbatim: 'our news-implied network includes about a third of the links in the Compustat Segments data' (top-50-by-sales subgraph). Entity-resolution loss verbatim: 'We lose about two-third of the firms in our sample when we restrict ourselves to firms that have a match in the merged CRSP / Compustat data set.' Stanford CoreNLP NER accuracy cited 'in the order of 80%'. Degree distribution power law exponent 1.83; median node 13 links, GM >21,000 links, min 1. Missing links concentrate in pharma distribution (BMY/PFE/ABC/MCK) because those links are not newsworthy — a systematic, not random, omission.

key_findings.claim: THE SINGLE MOST DECISION-RELEVANT COST RESULT: Ge, Li & Zheng (JBF 2025) ran every cross-firm momentum link type head-to-head WITH transaction costs. Only the news co-mention version survived. Customer momentum produced no positive return at all. Caveat: Chinese A-shares, weekly rebalance, retail-dominated — transferability to a US large-cap daily-ish cycle is unproven.
key_findings.numbers: Sample: all A-shares (SSE/SZSE/GEM), 2006-2020, weekly signal, ST shares excluded. Same-sentence identification, 3-month window: long-short 1.94%/mo [t=5.33], CH-4 alpha 1.86% [t=5.23]. After 16bps round-trip cost (Fan et al. 2021): 1.29% [t=3.56], CH-4 alpha 1.21% [t=3.42]. Verbatim: 'after taking transaction cost into consideration, trading strategies based on other cross-firm momentum effects all have insignificant alphas.' Pre-cost comparators: statistical-linkage 1.36% [t=3.93]; analyst co-coverage 0.86% [t=3.33] / CH-4 0.85% [t=2.97]; industry (Shenwan-1) 0.77% [t=3.25] / 0.76% [t=3.00]; technology 0.58% [t=2.73] / 0.60% [t=2.64]; concept 0.81% [t=2.25]. CUSTOMER MOMENTUM: 'only the customer momentum strategy does not yield positive returns or CH-4 alpha' — excluded from later analysis. Same-sentence beats same-article at equal window.

key_findings.claim: (e) ASKING AN LLM DIRECTLY IS NEAR-CHANCE on firm-pair supply links. On a BALANCED 50/50 benchmark against FactSet ground truth, GPT-5 zero-shot is barely above a coin flip. This is the strongest available evidence that LLM-named beneficiaries must be validated, never trusted.
key_findings.numbers: Ground truth: FactSet Supply Chain Relationships, 3,211 firms / 11,635 verified links, 2023 US public companies. Inductive test set 1,954 positives + 1,954 random negatives; fully-inductive 95 + 95. GPT-5 zero-shot: accuracy 0.555 / F 0.189 (inductive, no SIC), 0.566 / 0.229 (with SIC); fully inductive 0.526 / 0.096 and 0.532 / 0.129. DeepSeek-V3.1: 0.539 / 0.138 and 0.568 / 0.222. GPT-4o: 0.583 / 0.268. Trained InterCorpRel-LLM: 0.797-0.837 accuracy, F 0.829-0.854. GNN baselines GAT 0.753 acc / F 0.536, GraphSAGE 0.777 / 0.539 (and F=0.000 fully inductive). Authors: closed-source models 'nearly fail completely to identify true supply links'. CAVEAT to weigh: this is pairwise verification over random pairs, which is harder than open-ended 'name the beneficiaries of X' where the LLM's popularity prior helps — but it bounds how much you can trust an LLM-asserted A->B edge.

key_findings.claim: (e-variant) LLM + web-search-snippet extraction scales relationship COVERAGE far past disclosure-based data at low token cost, but the 2026 paper doing it reports NO precision, recall, F1 or hallucination rate at all — and the authors explicitly refuse to call the output ground truth.
key_findings.numbers: Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct over Serper search snippets, benchmarked against CSMAR (Chinese listed firms). Coverage: 7.2x more firms and 9.3x more relationships than CSMAR. Cost: 558 tokens per unique relation (snippets) vs 7,079 tokens per unique relation (full text); full text yields 19.8x more unique relations but needs 251.2x more input tokens. Duplicate rate 39.2% (snippets) vs 71.1% (full text). ZERO precision/recall/F1 reported. Verbatim limitation: output is 'a web-visible evidence graph rather than a complete transaction ledger' and 'absence from the graph should not be interpreted as absence of a real relationship'; relationships require 'downstream validation'.

key_findings.claim: (d) ETF HOLDINGS AS A FREE THEME BASKET: verified free and daily from at least two issuers, but a raw ETF basket is a weak portfolio and its coverage is biased toward already-trending sectors. Retrieval-augmented expansion beats the raw ETF basket by ~57% on Sharpe in the one paper that measured it.
key_findings.numbers: THEME/TRS dataset: 1,153 real-world thematic ETFs covering ~3,000 unique US equities; 969 kept after a min-10-constituent filter (678 train / 97 val / 194 test); expanded to ~200 unique themes using sector+industry classifications and news. Test window 2024-04-23 to 2025-04-29, 14-trading-day holding. RAW ETF baseline: Sharpe 0.4845, cumulative return 0.0672, MDD -0.2368. Best retrieval model @3: Sharpe 0.7592, CR 0.1645, MDD -0.2378. Retrieval quality: HR@3 0.5155 -> 0.8196; P@3 0.3522 -> 0.6289. Stated ETF bias: coverage 'is incomplete and biased toward trending sectors such as IT and clean energy'. MEASURED $0 access 2026-08-04: Global X publishes dated full-holdings CSV at https://assets.globalxetfs.com/funds/holdings/<ticker>_full-holdings_YYYYMMDD.csv (AIQ 2026-08-03 fetched, HTTP 200, 101 rows, includes % of net assets, ticker, name, SEDOL, shares, market value); SSGA XLK holdings xlsx HTTP 200. iShares' ajax CSV endpoint returned HTML (needs a different path).

key_findings.claim: (c) SEC EDGAR IS GENUINELY FREE AND SUFFICIENT for the disclosure route, and I verified the full-text search API works with no key. The legal hooks are SFAS 131 / ASC 280 (identity of any customer >10% of total sales) and Item 101 of Reg S-K (product descriptions — the same text TNIC parses). The binding limit is not access, it is that only ~232 US firms/month end up with a public LISTED customer.
key_findings.numbers: MEASURED 2026-08-04 with a plain curl + UA, no key: efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index returns HTTP 200. Full-text coverage starts 2001 — 10-K hits for the string 'customer': 1999 -> 6, 2000 -> 0, 2001 -> 8,658, 2002 -> 9,419. A targeted 2024 10-K query for 'accounted for approximately' returned 1,326 hits. data.sec.gov/submissions JSON API is free (used by arXiv 2606.29290 to pull 10-K MD&A). Cohen-Frazzini note that the dollar amount of sales to each customer is MISSING in about 19% of firm-year observations, and that pre-1998 customer names are abbreviations requiring soundex + hand matching.

key_findings.claim: A hand-curated 51-edge supply-chain graph was enough to produce a publishable-looking alpha on S&P500 names — which is either encouraging (you do not need FactSet-scale coverage) or a warning about overfitting a tiny graph. Treat as LOW confidence: single-author arXiv preprint, no transaction costs, no Compustat controls.
key_findings.numbers: 48 nodes / 51 directed edges, hand-built from 'regulatory filings, industry reports, and corporate disclosures', edge weights from estimated revenue dependence following Barrot-Sauvagnat (2016). 255 S&P 500 firms, 2011-2025, 24,723 firm-month observations. FinBERT embeddings of 10-K MD&A. net_pc_5 Newey-West t = -2.64; long-short annualized Sharpe 0.86; FF5 alpha 7.27%/yr [t=2.30]. Placebo (100 random edge reshuffles) one-sided p=0.000. Authors concede the KG is 'more limited in scope than commercial data products such as FactSet Supply Chain or Bloomberg SPLC' and that controls are price-derived, not balance-sheet.

key_findings.claim: BEA Input-Output tables are the free, canonical cross-SECTOR (not cross-firm) hop and are what VTNIC is built on top of. They are downloadable without a key, but the industry granularity will not resolve the operator's AI-datacenter case: 'computer and electronic products' is a single summary industry, and detail-level benchmark tables are published only every 5 years.
key_findings.numbers: MEASURED 2026-08-04: https://apps.bea.gov/industry/iTables%20Static%20Files/AllTablesSUP.zip HTTP 200, content-length 20,439,248, last-modified 2024-09-26. BEA API exists (free UserID required). Annual Make/Use tables cover 1997-2023 at ~71 summary industries; detail-level tables (~400 commodities) only at 5-year benchmark years. Schwenkler-Zheng's own criticism: BEA data 'are only updated once every 5 years and do not provide insights on firm-level connections'. FHP used 424 commodities / 426 industries from the 2002 Make table.

key_findings.claim: No free equivalent of FactSet SPLC / Bloomberg SPLC exists for public-equity firm-level supply-chain links — this was searched explicitly with a 2026-dated query and a year-less canonical query. Every serious 2024-2026 paper either buys FactSet, uses Compustat Segments (WRDS), or hand-builds a small graph.
key_findings.numbers: Commercial coverage benchmark for calibration: FactSet 3,211 firms / 11,635 verified links for 2023 US public companies (InterCorpRel-LLM). Compustat Segments (the free-ish legal-disclosure equivalent) yields only 232 focal firms/month with a listed customer (Ali-Hirshleifer) and 11,484 unique pairs over 25 years (Cohen-Frazzini). Ratio: FactSet has roughly an order of magnitude more usable firm-level links than the disclosure route.

key_findings.claim: LLM-based relationship extraction from unstructured text is precision-poor in the one study that reported real numbers, and the study that reported near-perfect numbers was measuring embedding-assisted classification on a clean structured automotive dataset, not open-world extraction. Do not conflate the two.
key_findings.numbers: Open-world relationship extraction from unstructured text: precision 0.449, recall 0.259, F1 0.328 (GPT-4o class model). Contrast: arXiv 2412.03390 reports ~1.0000/1.0000/1.0000 balanced-accuracy/precision/recall — but that is on a curated automotive dataset of 43,131 companies / 72 countries / 927 products split into 27 country-level sets, using small sentence encoders (all-MiniLM-L12-v2) to classify pre-formed quintuplets. That paper reports NO false-positive or hallucination rate and no GNN baseline comparison.

negative_or_null_results: Customer momentum (Cohen-Frazzini) is INSIGNIFICANT value-weighted post-discovery: 0.62%/mo t=1.54 in 2005-2018 vs 1.30% t=3.03 in 1978-2004 (Pinchuk 2023). The EW FF5+UMD alpha also falls to t=1.89.

Customer momentum's 4-factor alpha collapses from 0.97 (t=2.47) to 0.43 (t=1.09) once shared-analyst-coverage (CF) momentum is controlled for. Supplier-industry, customer-industry, industry, geographic and technology momentum all go insignificant or NEGATIVE after the same control (Ali & Hirshleifer, JFE 2020).
In the only head-to-head test with transaction costs, EVERY cross-firm momentum link type EXCEPT news co-mention had insignificant alphas after a 16bps round-trip cost (Ge, Li & Zheng, JBF 2025).
Customer momentum produced NO positive return or CH-4 alpha at all in Chinese A-shares — the authors dropped it from the study, blaming customer-disclosure quality (same JBF 2025 paper).
Hoberg-Phillips TNIC is EXPLICITLY purged of vertical relationships (readme, verbatim). It cannot express a theme->supplier hop. It is a competitor map.

VTNIC (the vertical version) has NEVER been validated for return prediction. Its published validation is against 10-K self-statements of vertical integration and Census related-party trade — an M&A/organization test, not an asset-pricing test. It also measures POTENTIAL vertical relatedness from BEA vocabulary overlap, not observed trade flows.
VTNIC's usable file is 'top 10% of all pairwise scores' — meaning ~10% of random firm pairs are flagged related. For beneficiary SELECTION that is an enormous false-positive surface.
Both TNIC and VTNIC ship gvkey-only. No ticker, no CIK, no permno. The official crosswalk is a Compustat/WRDS product.

Schwenkler & Zheng's news-implied network recovers only ~1/3 of Compustat-Segments customer-supplier links, and the misses are SYSTEMATIC (pharma distribution links are not newsworthy), not random. They also lose ~2/3 of firms to CRSP/Compustat name matching.

Schwenkler & Zheng report NO precision/recall anywhere — the words do not appear in the paper. Their result is aggregate-risk prediction (VIX, BAA-AAA, default rate, IP growth), not cross-sectional stock alpha.

GPT-5 zero-shot on a BALANCED supply-link classification benchmark scores accuracy 0.555 and F 0.189 — essentially a coin flip on a 50/50 task. DeepSeek-V3.1 F=0.138. GPT-4o F=0.268. Trained model: F=0.854.
The 2026 LLM-plus-search-snippet supply-chain pipeline reports zero precision, recall, F1, or hallucination rate, and its authors explicitly say absence from the graph is not evidence of absence.

Raw thematic-ETF baskets are a WEAK portfolio: Sharpe 0.4845 / CR 0.0672 over 2024-04 to 2025-04, and ETF coverage is admittedly 'biased toward trending sectors such as IT and clean energy' — i.e. ETF holdings will tell you about the AI theme AFTER it is consensus, which is exactly the wrong side of a slow-thematic trade.

BEA I-O detail tables (~400 commodities) are published only at 5-year benchmark years; annual tables are ~71 summary industries. 'Memory makers vs cooling vs transformers' does not exist as separate industries at annual granularity.
EDGAR full-text search does not reach before 2001 (measured: 0 10-K hits in 2000, 8,658 in 2001). Any backtest needing pre-2001 filing text cannot use the free FTS API.
Cohen-Frazzini themselves report the dollar amount of sales to each customer is missing in ~19% of firm-year observations, and pre-1998 customer identities require phonetic + hand matching.
recommendation_for_pyfinagent:
Build the beneficiary map as a CANDIDATE GENERATOR plus a THREE-WAY CORROBORATION GATE, and do not build the customer-supplier momentum signal at all.

P0 (prerequisite, already a measured gap): create the BigQuery tables news_articles and news_sentiment that backend/news/bq_writer.py silently no-ops into, and backfill from the Alpha Vantage NEWS_SENTIMENT archive (key present; archive confirmed to at least 2022-02-24). Nothing below is backtestable until a news corpus is persisted and at least one news-derived column lands in the backtest engine's _NUMERIC_FEATURES (currently 37 features, zero from news). Without this, any beneficiary work is un-gate-able exactly like news_screen is today.

LAYER 1 - candidate generation (cycle-level, ~one LLM call per theme, not per ticker):
(1) NEWS CO-MENTION GRAPH from the Alpha Vantage archive. This is the highest-value build in this lens. Rationale: it is the ONLY cross-firm link type that survived transaction costs in the one head-to-head study (1.29%/mo t=3.56 net of 16bps; every other link type insignificant), and AV already returns per-article ticker tags with relevance AND sentiment scores — which eliminates the two failures that crippled Schwenkler-Zheng (80%-accurate NER, and losing 2/3 of firms to name matching). Edge weight = sum over articles of relevance_i * relevance_j. Use same-ARTICLE co-tagging (AV does not expose sentence offsets); note the China paper found same-SENTENCE strictly better, so expect a haircut. Identification window 3 months (their best), and the sign convention is a lead-lag on the linked firm's return, not sentiment.
(2) VTNIC 10%-granularity as a STRUCTURAL PRIOR, not a signal. Download VertNetwork_10gran.zip (854MB, free, no auth). Resolve gvkey via the free farr gvkey_ciks table (78,339 rows) -> CIK -> ticker via SEC company_tickers.json, and MEASURE the join hit rate against the live universe before trusting it; treat any name that fails to resolve as absent, never as unrelated. Use only the directed upstream/downstream flag plus rank, refreshed annually.
(3) THEMATIC ETF CO-MEMBERSHIP from free daily holdings CSVs (Global X pattern verified working; SSGA verified). Use as a "does the market already call this a theme member" indicator — which is deliberately a LAGGING confirmation, useful as a corroborator and useless as an edge.
(4) LLM AS HYPOTHESIS GENERATOR ONLY: one cycle-level call per theme, "name plausible second-order beneficiaries of <theme> and the mechanism". Cheap and high-recall. NEVER let its output reach a score directly — GPT-5 scores F=0.19 on verified pairwise supply links.

LAYER 2 - the gate. A candidate ticker enters the theme basket only if at least 2 of the 3 INDEPENDENT free corroborators fire: (i) a VTNIC directed vertical link to a named theme anchor, (ii) a news co-mention count above a pre-registered threshold in the identification window, (iii) thematic-ETF co-membership. Log which corroborators fired per name so the attribution is auditable, mirroring the existing overlay pattern.

LAYER 3 - promotion. Ship it as a new apply_*_to_score overlay routed through overlay_math.py::sign_safe_mult, DEFAULT OFF, exactly like defense_signal.py. Emit the corroboration count and the co-mention lead-lag as numeric features into _NUMERIC_FEATURES so the immutable gates can actually run. Then require the full gate: DSR>=0.95, PBO<=0.5, beat incumbent OOS, clears costs. Cost realism is the binding constraint, not signal discovery — pre-register a turnover cap and re-run the gate at 16bps and at 30bps round-trip, because the literature says every one of these effects except news co-mention dies at 16bps.

Explicitly do NOT build: a Cohen-Frazzini customer-momentum overlay. Post-2005 VW alpha is insignificant, only ~232 US names/month have the link at $1.5B average cap (outside the S&P500/Russell1000 universe), the effect is subsumed by an analyst-link factor that needs paid I/B/E/S, and the pre-2006 data availability cliff means you cannot even build a modern factor from public disclosure. The four reference cases (COVID/pharma, AI/datacenter, Ukraine/defense, Iran/oil) are all NEWS-PROPAGATED themes, not customer-disclosure-propagated ones — the co-mention graph is the mechanism-matched instrument, and defense_signal.py is the existing proof that the hard-coded single-theme version works. Generalize defense_signal.py's shape (macro/theme trigger AND basket momentum confirmation) rather than inventing a new architecture.

Finally, respect the call_transcript_gpr.py precedent: if the theme-beneficiary feature turns out contemporaneous-only with no forward predictability, scope it as a risk filter and say so in the docstring rather than shipping it as alpha.
rejected_options: BUY FactSet SPLC / Bloomberg SPLC / Mergent Supply Chain — violates the $0 metered constraint outright. Included only as the coverage benchmark (3,211 firms / 11,635 links for 2023 US names).

Hoberg-Phillips TNIC3 as the beneficiary map — REJECTED on the readme's own words: TNIC is 'purged for vertical relationships from the input/output tables'. It returns competitors. Using it for a theme->supplier hop would be a category error, and TNIC3 is also the file most people reach for by default.

Compustat Segments customer links (the Cohen-Frazzini data) — rejected twice over: the WRDS product is paid, and the free EDGAR-parsed reconstruction only yields ~232 usable focal firms/month at $1.5B average cap, which barely intersects a 500-1000 large/mid-cap universe.
Rebuilding customer momentum as a live overlay — rejected on measured post-publication decay (VW t=1.54) plus subsumption by analyst-link momentum (t falls to 1.09).

Shared analyst coverage (Ali-Hirshleifer CF momentum, alpha 1.68% t=9.67, IR 1.71) — the strongest link type in the US literature, but it requires I/B/E/S analyst-coverage data. No free source found. Rejected on the $0 constraint, not on merit. Worth flagging to the operator as the single most valuable PAID dataset if the constraint ever relaxes.

BEA I-O tables alone as the beneficiary map — free but too coarse: ~71 summary industries annually, detail (~400 commodities) only every 5 years. Cannot separate memory / power / cooling / transformers inside 'computer and electronic products'. Keep it only as the substrate VTNIC already uses.

Building our own 10-K co-mention/supply-chain NER pipeline from EDGAR-CORPUS or BeanCounter — rejected on effort-vs-return: the published open-world extraction numbers are precision 0.449 / recall 0.259 / F1 0.328, and Alpha Vantage already ships ticker-tagged news with relevance scores at $0, which skips the whole entity-resolution problem that cost Schwenkler-Zheng two-thirds of their firms.
Trusting an LLM to name beneficiaries without corroboration — rejected on GPT-5 F=0.189-0.229 (accuracy 0.555 on a balanced 50/50 task) against FactSet ground truth.

Buying a thematic ETF basket directly, or using ETF holdings as the primary generator — rejected: raw ETF baskets scored Sharpe 0.4845 in the one measured test, and holdings are admittedly biased toward already-trending sectors, so they confirm a theme after the move rather than before it. Demoted to corroborator.
Finnhub / Benzinga news sources — API keys are absent (measured), so they are not a $0 path without new signups; Alpha Vantage is already keyed and archived.
open_questions: What is the actual join hit rate from the free gvkey->CIK->ticker chain (farr gvkey_ciks, 78,339 rows) onto pyfinagent's live 500-1000 name universe? If it is below ~90%, VTNIC's value as a corroborator degrades sharply and the failures will not be random. This must be MEASURED before VTNIC is designed in, not assumed.

Does the Alpha Vantage NEWS_SENTIMENT archive expose enough per-article structure to approximate SAME-SENTENCE co-mention, or only same-article? The China paper found same-sentence strictly dominates same-article at every window length, so this determines the expected haircut. Needs a live probe of the AV response schema.

How far back does the AV archive actually go, ticker by ticker? The brief states 'at least 2022-02-24'. A ~4-year sample with weekly-to-monthly rebalancing gives very few independent observations for a DSR>=0.95 / PBO<=0.5 gate. Is the effective sample large enough to clear the promotion gate at all, or does this feature need to wait until the corpus accumulates?

Does the news co-mention result transfer from Chinese A-shares (retail-dominated, weekly rebalance, 2006-2020) to US large/mid caps on a daily-ish cycle? The published US news co-occurrence number I found is a 68bps/month alpha, roughly a third of the China figure, and I could not read that paper in full (EFMA host had a TLS certificate failure). This is the biggest unverified transfer assumption in the recommendation.

Has anyone published a return-predictability test using VTNIC? I found none — FHP's own paper is about vertical M&A and integration, with no asset-pricing test. If nobody has tested it, that is either an untapped edge or a silent graveyard of null results.

What is the correct null/benchmark for a corroboration gate at 10% VTNIC granularity? With 10% of random pairs flagged related, a naive 2-of-3 rule may pass mostly noise. The gate thresholds need to be pre-registered against a randomized-theme placebo (the arXiv 2606.29290 edge-reshuffle placebo, p=0.000, is the pattern to copy).

Coverage-year conflict on the free TNIC files: hobergphillips industryclass.htm says 1989-2021 while the library index says 1989-2023, and the tnic3 zip was last modified 2024-11-20 while VertNetwork_all.zip was refreshed 2026-06-05. The actual max year in each file should be read from the data, not from the web page.

Does the operator want the second-order hop to be MECHANISM-typed (supplier vs power consumer vs cooling vs financier)? Hilt & Schwenkler (2025, SSRN 4946066, 403 to WebFetch) separate news co-mentions into distinct relationship types; if beneficiary MECHANISM matters for sizing or for explaining the four reference cases, that paper is the one to obtain next.

lens: LENS 3 — TIMING AND CROWDING: where in a theme's life cycle the tradable edge sits (birth / acceleration / confirmation), and the quantified decay.
bottom_line: The edge is in ACCELERATION, not birth or confirmation, and it lives entirely in SECOND-order names: the directly-named firm prices its own shock essentially fully within the event month (Cohen-Frazzini underreaction coefficient 0.939, t not different from 1), while the economically-linked firm prices only ~60% immediately and closes the remaining ~40% over the next 6 months (URC 0.600, t=5.71; CAR[t+1,t+6] = +2.80%, t=3.74). Enter on a RISING 6-month theme-attention trend with beneficiaries chosen by return-beta to the theme (6.96%/yr alpha, t=2.53), hold 6 months, hard-cap 12; exit on any crowding trigger. Crowding is a real and published top signal: specialized/thematic ETFs deliver -0.50%/mo FFC4 alpha (t=-4.02) for 60 months post-launch, cumulatively about -30%, and the effect vanishes after month 60 (-0.12%/mo, t=-1.56) — the damage is entirely the post-launch window, and a stock-level long of new specialized ETFs' top-5 holdings underperforms by a similar magnitude, which is precisely the naive "buy the named theme beneficiaries" trade.

key_findings.claim: FIRST-order vs SECOND-order is the cleanest quantified split in the literature. The named/first-order firm (the customer whose news moved) fully prices its own shock in the event month: underreaction coefficient URC = 0.939 (t=1.53, not statistically different from 1) and cumulative return over t+1..t+6 of only 0.442% (t=1.59, insignificant). The second-order firm (the economically linked supplier) covers only ~60% of the gap in month 0 and closes the remaining ~40% over the FOLLOWING SIX MONTHS: URC = 0.600 (t=5.71), CAR[t+1,t+6] = +2.799% (t=3.74). Long-short customer-momentum FF3 alpha = 1.555%/mo (t=3.60) value-weighted, 1.306%/mo (t=4.67) equal-weighted; 4-factor 1.376%/mo (t=3.13); 5-factor incl. Pastor-Stambaugh liquidity 1.237%/mo (t=2.99). Supplier prices rise 3.9% in month 0 while the sales-weighted customer portfolio jumps 7.8%. Cumulative 4.73% over the subsequent year; the paper states the predictable returns 'persist for about a year and then fade away'.
key_findings.numbers: URC customer 0.939 (t=1.53); URC supplier 0.600 (t=5.71); CAR[t+1,t+6] +2.799% (t=3.74); CCAR customer +0.442% (t=1.59); FF3 alpha 1.555%/mo VW (t=3.60), 1.306%/mo EW (t=4.67); 4-factor 1.376 (t=3.13); 5-factor 1.237 (t=2.99); month-0 move 3.9% supplier vs 7.8% customer; +4.73% cumulative over year 1; sample 1981-2004, 288 months, 11,484 unique supplier-customer links, avg customer = 19.8% of supplier sales

key_findings.claim: CRITICAL FOR OUR UNIVERSE — large caps get the SAME total second-order alpha but it arrives FASTER, so the usable window is shorter. Large firms cover 69% of the gap in month 0 (URC 0.689, t=3.89), leaving only 31% to accrue over 6 months; small firms cover just 35% (URC 0.348, t=8.15), leaving 65%. The paper states explicitly: 'Although the customer momentum total abnormal return is roughly the same in large and small cap securities, prices tend to converge faster for large cap stocks.' Since pyfinagent's universe is S&P500/Russell1000 large-mid cap, plan for the ~31% residual profile, not the 65% one.
key_findings.numbers: URC larger firms 0.689 (t=3.89) => 31% residual over 6 months; URC smaller firms 0.348 (t=8.15) => 65% residual; total abnormal return roughly equal across size

key_findings.claim: The second-order effect is CROSS-INDUSTRY and does NOT require speed — both facts are decisive for pyfinagent's design and constraints. 78% of firm-customer links are between firms in DIFFERENT industries, and results are robust to industry adjustment. On implementability: delaying entry by a full week or a full MONTH does not kill the signal — skip-a-week L/S = 1.377%/mo VW (t=3.16) / 1.046%/mo EW (t=3.14); skip-a-MONTH = 1.464%/mo VW (t=3.55) / 0.932%/mo EW (t=3.28). A daily decision cycle is therefore fully adequate; no low-latency infrastructure is needed. NOTE the existing peer_leadlag_screen.py groups by GICS sector and so is structurally unable to express this cross-sector hop.
key_findings.numbers: 78% of links cross-industry; skip-a-week 1.377%/mo VW (t=3.16), 1.046 EW (t=3.14); skip-a-month 1.464%/mo VW (t=3.55), 0.932 EW (t=3.28); baseline liquid-stock 1.578 VW (t=3.79), 1.311 EW (t=4.93)

key_findings.claim: CROWDING — YES, there is published evidence that thematic/specialized ETF inception marks the peak, and it is strong. Specialized ETFs (sector/industry + thematic) earn FFC4 alpha of -0.27%/mo (t=-3.30) overall (-3.24%/yr), but -0.50%/mo (t=-4.02) = about -6%/yr during the first 60 months, cumulating to approximately -30% risk-adjusted over five years. After month 60 the underperformance is -0.12%/mo (t=-1.56), statistically indistinguishable from zero — i.e. the entire loss is the post-launch window. Fees explain almost none of it: the specialized-vs-broad fee gap is only 0.13%/yr against a ~-3%/yr alpha gap. The underlying stocks ran up beforehand (market-adjusted return months -24..-6: 1.04%/mo specialized vs 0.66%/mo broad, difference 0.38%/mo, t=4.15) and carried extreme attention and valuation (media exposure difference +37.37, t=4.29; media sentiment difference +0.42, t=3.98; price-to-sales 28.83 vs 9.29, difference 19.54, t=2.75; 20.10% vs 12.20% negative-earnings firms, t=7.20). The paper's own words: 'By the time an eligible sector or theme is identified by ETF issuers based on its popularity, the valuation cycle has already peaked. After launch, valuations start sliding downward.' Sector/industry and thematic index performance REVERSES the pre-launch run-up (smart-beta merely flattens to zero alpha).
key_findings.numbers: FFC4 -0.27%/mo (t=-3.30) all months; months<=60: -0.50%/mo (t=-4.02) = -6%/yr, cumulative ~-30%; months>60: -0.12%/mo (t=-1.56) n.s.; Sp-minus-BB months<=60 -0.37%/mo (t=-2.61); fee gap 0.13%/yr; pre-launch run-up 1.04 vs 0.66%/mo (diff 0.38, t=4.15); sample 1,080 US equity ETFs 2000-2019, 526 specialized (411 sector/industry, 115 thematic)

key_findings.claim: THE SINGLE MOST DANGEROUS RESULT FOR OUR PROPOSED DESIGN. Ben-David et al. Appendix Table F.6 runs a STOCK-LEVEL strategy that is long the top five holdings of specialized ETFs launched in the previous 12 months and finds 'a similar magnitude of underperformance' to the ETF-level result. That is almost exactly the trade our theme->beneficiary mapping would generate if beneficiaries are selected the way ETF issuers select them (salient, attention-grabbing, recently-run-up names). Furthermore, within the specialized category the ETFs whose underlying stocks had the HIGHEST pre-launch returns and media sentiment perform WORST: -0.53%/mo FFC4 (-0.58% split by returns, -0.48% split by media sentiment), versus -0.20%/mo for those launched after LOWER pre-launch returns and sentiment (-0.01% and -0.38% respectively). Ranking candidate beneficiaries by recent run-up plus positive media sentiment is therefore an ANTI-signal at this horizon.
key_findings.numbers: top-5-holdings stock-level strategy: 'similar magnitude of underperformance'; highest pre-launch return+sentiment specialized ETFs -0.53%/mo FFC4 (-0.58% / -0.48%); lowest -0.20%/mo (-0.01% / -0.38%); media sentiment and market-to-book 'quickly revert to lower levels' within the year after launch

key_findings.claim: THE BEST-CALIBRATED ENTRY RULE FOUND, and it is a theme-level attention TREND, not a shock. Across 347 narratives quantified from 150k+ digital media sources (roughly 5-7 million articles/week), 2013-2023, Russell 3000: sorting narratives on the 6-MONTH attention-intensity difference (trailing 6-month average intensity minus the prior 6-month average) and holding 6 months yields a Fama-French 6-factor alpha of 6.96%/yr (t=2.53), robust across holding horizons from 1 to 9 months. It is NOT price momentum in disguise: after double-sorting on 6-month past returns the portfolio still earns 5.37%/yr (t=2.17) with 6.38%/yr alpha (t=2.56). The authors' interpretation matches our operator's thesis exactly: investors respond to short-run narrative shocks but 'under-react to long-run narrative trends'. Decomposition: most of the spread is intra-sector (4.69%/yr, t=1.95; alpha 5.69%, t=2.31), with a smaller but highly significant genuine cross-SECTOR component (1.46%/yr, t=2.59; alpha 1.51%, t=2.82).
key_findings.numbers: 6M intensity difference + 6M holding: alpha 6.96%/yr (t=2.53); momentum-controlled 5.37%/yr return (t=2.17), 6.38%/yr alpha (t=2.56); intra-sector 4.69%/yr (t=1.95), alpha 5.69% (t=2.31); cross-sector 1.46%/yr (t=2.59), alpha 1.51% (t=2.82); 347 narratives, 2013-2023, long-short top/bottom 25 stocks by narrative beta, monthly rebalance, betas from rolling 52 weekly observations

key_findings.claim: HOW to pick beneficiaries — a decisive null that invalidates the obvious LLM approach. Lee/Ozik/Sadka form narrative-mimicking portfolios two ways: (a) by narrative BETA (return co-movement with the theme's attention series), and (b) by taking the top-25 stocks with the HIGHEST media coverage of that narrative regardless of beta. Method (a) works. Method (b) 'do[es] not exhibit abnormal returns.' Being NAMED in theme coverage carries no alpha; statistically co-moving with the theme does. Conditional on beta selection, high-media-coverage stocks give the strongest result (6.98%/yr return, 8.98%/yr alpha), so coverage is a useful conditioner but a useless primary selector. This means an LLM that reads news and names 'who benefits' reproduces the failing method (b) — and method (b) is also what ETF issuers do (see the -30%/5yr finding).
key_findings.numbers: highest-media-coverage-selected narrative portfolios: no abnormal returns (null); beta-selected within high-media-coverage subset: 6.98%/yr return, 8.98%/yr FF6 alpha; ~1900 stocks with zero coverage vs ~1000 with any coverage per month across 347 narratives

key_findings.claim: THE DECAY CURVE, from the 2026 frontier paper (recency-scan hit). Purging news embeddings of the component predictable from prevailing stock characteristics yields 'pure news', which more than doubles raw news's predictive power. Decay: the no-delay strategy earns about 30%/yr on 10% volatility (essentially all CAPM alpha); predictability 'drops by roughly half after one month' and takes 'at least a year and a half before the predictive content of news becomes insignificant'. So the half-life is about ONE MONTH and the terminal horizon is about 18 MONTHS. Turnover of the 1-month version is 75% one-sided, which EXCEEDS every JKP factor (highest is short-term reversal at 67%) — the fast version is cost-hostile, vindicating the operator's decision to drop fast headline trading.
