Burst test: 40 sequential calls in 6.1s (~6.5/s) -> 40 OK, 0 errors, no 429, no key. Moat et al. used stats.grok.se from 2007-12-10, a now-discontinued separate system.

key_findings.claim: The published finance evidence for Wikipedia pageviews is real but weak for OUR use: the effect is INDEX-level (DJIA), CONTRARIAN in sign, concentrated in the 2008 crisis year, and the authors explicitly excluded transaction costs. It is not cross-sectional stock selection and does not support a thematic-beneficiary signal.
key_findings.numbers: Period 10 Dec 2007-30 Apr 2012, delta-t=3 weeks. Random strategy (10,000 realisations): mean return=0.0002, V=25012353, p=0.97. 30 DJIA-company pages VIEWS: mean R=0.50 SD, W=199690, p=0.005. 285 financial-topic pages VIEWS: mean R=1.10 SD, W=2286608, p<0.001. Directional: after a DECREASE in views, mean DJIA weekly return=+0.0027 (V=39592, p<0.001); after an INCREASE, -0.0021 (V=2222, p<0.001) — views up implies returns DOWN. Year-by-year mean returns in SDs: 2008=0.89, 2009=0.19, 2010=0.19, 2011=0.55 (chi2=129.49, df=3, p<0.001) — effect ~4.7x larger in the crisis year than 2009/2010. Robust across delta-t 1-10 weeks (all p<0.001). Placebo: 233 actor/filmmaker pages.

key_findings.claim: COMPUTED DSR/PBO feasibility: free history is NOT the binding constraint on the gates. At GDELT's measured 2,885 trading days, a strategy needs annualised Sharpe >=1.23 to clear DSR>=0.95 after 100 trials — demanding but achievable. The real trap is the CSCV configuration: at monthly rebalancing the S=16 splits used by mcp__pyfinagent-risk__pbo_check leave only 8.6 observations per split, which is unusable.
key_findings.numbers: Min annualised Sharpe for DSR>=0.95 (Bailey/Lopez de Prado, gaussian moments): GDELT T=2885 daily -> N=1:0.49, N=20:1.05, N=100:1.23, N=500:1.39. Same at weekly T=596 -> 1.24 at N=100. Monthly T=137 -> 1.26 at N=100. AlphaVantage dense-era-only T=67 -> 1.83 at N=100 (infeasible). EDGAR T=295 -> 0.85 at N=100. GPR T=499 -> 0.65 at N=100. CSCV S=16 obs/split: monthly=8.6 UNUSABLE, weekly=37.2 OK, daily=180.3 OK, AlphaVantage-dense=4.2 UNUSABLE.

key_findings.claim: The honest binding constraint is independent THEMATIC EPISODES, not bytes or dollars. GDELT's 11.46-year window contains only ~23-46 big cross-sector themes at 2-4/year. No paid vendor fixes this — it is a property of the world. GPR (1985+) and EDGAR (2001+) are the only ways to buy more episodes, and they cost $0.
key_findings.numbers: Episodes at 2/yr and 4/yr: GDELT GKG (11.46y measured) = 23-46; Wikipedia pageviews (11.1y) = 22-44; EDGAR FTS (25.6y) = 51-102; GPR daily (41.6y) = 83-166. The operator's own four reference cases (COVID, AI/datacenter, Ukraine, Iran/oil) are 4 episodes in 6 years, consistent with the ~2/yr end of that range.

negative_or_null_results: NULL RESULT (Moat et al. 2013, read in full): Wikipedia EDIT volume has NO predictive relationship with DJIA returns, twice. DJIA-company pages: mean R = -0.09, W=140781, p>0.9. 285 financial-topic pages: mean R = 0.12, W=1516626, p=0.19. The authors attribute this to data volume (financial pages averaged 1,351,796 views each but only 431 edits; 43 of 285 pages had ZERO edits) and drop edits from the study. Any design proposing edit-count features should be rejected on this evidence.

NEGATIVE RESULT (Moat et al.): the pageview effect is concentrated in the 2008 crisis year — mean returns by year in SDs of the random strategy were 2008=0.89 vs 2009=0.19, 2010=0.19, 2011=0.55. The 2009/2010 effect is ~4.7x smaller than 2008. A signal whose measured edge is dominated by one crisis year is a poor candidate for a strict OOS-robustness gate.

NEGATIVE RESULT (Moat et al., author's own caveat, verbatim): "we neglect transaction fees, since the maximum number of transactions per year when using this strategy is only 104... We note that inclusion of transaction fees would of course diminish any profit if this hypothetical strategy were to be used in the real world." The headline result is a gross-of-cost result and our gate requires clearing costs.

NEGATIVE RESULT: the Wikipedia signal's SIGN is contrarian and index-level, not a thematic-beneficiary long signal. Following an INCREASE in financial-page views the DJIA returned -0.0021 the next week (p<0.001); following a DECREASE, +0.0027 (p<0.001). Attention UP predicts returns DOWN. This is a risk/deleveraging indicator, structurally similar to call_transcript_gpr.py's existing role — i.e. it risks repeating the exact failure mode the brief says must not be repeated.

NEGATIVE RESULT (measured): Wikimedia pageviews only start 2015-07-01. The founding evidence (Moat et al.) used 2007-12-10 to 2012-04-30 via the now-discontinued stats.grok.se. There is therefore ZERO overlap between the published evidence window and the data we can actually obtain — the result cannot be replicated or extended on our data, only assumed to persist.

NEGATIVE RESULT (measured): Alpha Vantage NEWS_SENTIMENT's deep archive is illusory as backtest input. AAPL had 5 indexed articles in Jan-2013 and 53 in Jan-2025 but >=1000 in Jan-2026. The archive is a sparse retroactive backfill that does not reproduce what a live subscriber would have seen, which is a first-order point-in-time integrity failure independent of the licence and rate-limit problems.

NEGATIVE RESULT (measured): Alpaca returns hasContent=False for 2016 archive articles even with include_content=true, and its `source` field returns an empty string rather than "Benzinga". Only headlines are reliably available historically, so any body-text-based theme extraction on Alpaca history will silently degrade to headline-only.

NEGATIVE/COST RESULT (measured): BigQuery LIMIT does not reduce scan cost. `SELECT DATE, V2Themes FROM gdelt-bq.gdeltv2.gkg LIMIT 10` scans 1.88 TB — a single exploratory query would consume 188% of the monthly 1 TiB free tier. This is a live $0-constraint tripwire for anyone exploring GDELT interactively.

NULL RESULT (my own coverage gap): I could not retrieve the FRED API terms of use. https://fred.stlouisfed.org/docs/api/terms_of_use.html returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch and HTTP 000 to curl with a browser UA across three URL variants; fred.stlouisfed.org/legal also 403'd. The FRED derived-works/commercial clause and the third-party-copyright carve-out remain UNVERIFIED. I am reporting this rather than asserting the commonly-repeated 'FRED is public domain' claim, which is only reliably true for US-government-produced series.

NULL RESULT: I found no published accuracy audit of GDELT's GKG V2Themes field specifically. The ~55% figure is measured on EVENT records (actor/event-type fields from the CAMEO coder), which is a different pipeline from the GKG theme taxonomy we would actually use. Applying the 55% number to V2Themes would be an unmeasured extrapolation.

NEGATIVE RESULT: Alpaca's documentation contains no licence grant for derived works. Neither docs/historical-news-data nor the API reference states redistribution or derived-signal terms, and the content is third-party Benzinga-licensed. Absence of a permissive grant is not permission.
recommendation_for_pyfinagent:
RANKED TABLE (1 = build on it now):

1. SEC EDGAR full-text search — history 2001+ (MEASURED floor), latency real-time-as-filed, limit 10 req/s (~864k/day, ~1000x headroom), PIT integrity BEST-IN-CLASS (accessioned filings are immutable, zero revision risk), licence US-government public domain with NO derived-signal restriction, extraction cost trivial. THIS IS THE SLEEPER. It is the only free source that is deep + PIT-clean + firm-level + public-domain simultaneously, and 10-K/10-Q Item 1A/Item 7 text is literally firms describing their own thematic exposures. It is the natural substrate for the cross-sector theme->beneficiary map that the brief says does not exist anywhere in the codebase. Its quarterly/annual cadence is a FEATURE for a weeks-to-months channel, not a bug.

2. Caldara-Iacoviello GPR — history 1985 daily / 1900 monthly, 44 countries, licence CC-BY (derived commercial signals explicitly permitted), PIT integrity GOOD *only if* you pin vintages. MANDATORY: consume data_gpr_daily_recent_YYYYMMDD.xls vintages, never the live file — the page states published values are revised backward. Also handle the 2021 search-term methodology break (GPR_OLD vs current) as a regime split, not a continuous series. Already fetched by defense_signal.py, so the ingestion path exists. Watch the latency: the DAILY series updates only WEEKLY (Mondays), so a daily cycle carries up to 7 days of staleness — do not treat GPR daily as a same-day input.

3. GDELT (gkg_partitioned ONLY) — history 2015-02-17..2026-08-04, 4,169 measured daily partitions, 15-min latency, licence unlimited commercial. Use as a THEME-INTENSITY series only, never for firm-level events; that is precisely what the peer-reviewed comparison recommends. HARD RULE: always query `gdelt-bq.gdeltv2.gkg_partitioned` with a `_PARTITIONTIME` filter. Never touch `gdeltv2.gkg` — one V2Themes query there scans 1.88 TB and blows 188% of the monthly free tier. Daily incremental is 379 MB/day (~11.4 GB/month), comfortably inside the 1 TiB free tier; the full 11.5-year backfill is ~1.58 TB, so run it across two calendar months to stay at literally $0, or accept ~$3.60 once. Deduplication is mandatory before use (the ~20.6% redundancy is a virality-correlated BIAS, not averaging noise).

4. FRED — keep for macro control variables, and USE ALFRED VINTAGES (`realtime_start`/`realtime_end`), not current values. 1,221 vintages for INDPRO back to 1927-01-26 (measured). This is the correct antidote to the macro-revision lookahead class this codebase has already been bitten by. Verify the terms-of-use page before any commercial framing — I could not retrieve it.

5. Alpaca news — usable as a LIVE forward-collection feed only (2015+ floor measured, 200 calls/min, Benzinga-sourced). Do NOT build the historical layer on it: headlines-only for the archive, and no licence grant for derived works. Acceptable as a live corroboration input; not gate-bearing evidence.

6. Wikimedia pageviews — cheap to add (no key, ~6.5 req/s measured, CC0, 2015-07-01 floor) but ONLY as an attention/risk-filter covariate with a CONTRARIAN prior, never as a thematic long signal. Budget it as a nice-to-have, not a dependency.

7. Alpha Vantage NEWS_SENTIMENT — DO NOT BUILD ON IT. Three independent disqualifiers, any one of which is fatal: (a) licence restricts to "personal, non-commercial use" and names "investment analysis, research, testing" as commercial; (b) MEASURED 25 requests/day makes universe backfill take 400+ days; (c) the pre-2026 archive is a sparse retroactive backfill (>=19x density discontinuity) and is therefore PIT-invalid. Note the key IS present in backend/.env, so this needs an explicit "do not use" decision, not silence.

LICENCE FLAGS (explicitly answering the brief): Alpha Vantage FORBIDS our use — hard flag, operator decision required. Alpaca/Benzinga is UNRESOLVED — no grant found; treat as flagged. GDELT (unlimited commercial), GPR (CC-BY), EDGAR (public domain) and Wikimedia (CC0) are all CLEAR for derived commercial signals. FRED is UNVERIFIED (page unreachable).

DSR/PBO ANSWER: free history does NOT cap us below the gates. At GDELT's 2,885 trading days a strategy needs annualised Sharpe >=1.23 to clear DSR>=0.95 after 100 trials; on GPR's 41 years it needs only 0.65. Two concrete configuration consequences: (i) rebalance WEEKLY, not monthly — at monthly frequency the S=16 CSCV splits in mcp__pyfinagent-risk__pbo_check get 8.6 observations each, which cannot produce a stable PBO estimate (weekly gives 37.2, daily 180.3); (ii) pre-register and CAP the trial count, because the Sharpe hurdle climbs from 0.49 (N=1) to 1.39 (N=500) on identical data — the trial budget, not the data budget, is what will actually fail this gate.

THE HONEST CAVEAT: the real ceiling is ~23-46 independent cross-sector thematic episodes in GDELT's window (the operator's own four reference cases are 4 episodes in 6 years). Rows are plentiful; episodes are not. A DSR computed on daily returns will look far more significant than the ~30 effective episodes justify. Recommend defining the unit of analysis as the EPISODE and reporting an episode-level significance figure alongside the daily-return DSR, otherwise the gate will pass on a technicality. Extending the sample to EDGAR (2001+, 51-102 episodes) or GPR (1985+, 83-166 episodes) is the only lever that actually buys statistical power — and both cost $0.
rejected_options: Alpha Vantage NEWS_SENTIMENT as the historical news corpus — REJECTED on three independent fatal grounds: licence restricts to personal non-commercial use with 'investment analysis, research, testing' explicitly named as commercial; a MEASURED hard limit of 25 requests/day making a 500-ticker backfill take 400+ days; and a >=19x archive-vs-live density discontinuity making it point-in-time invalid. Note this reverses the brief's implicit assumption that the held key made it usable.

GDELT for firm-level or event-level signals — REJECTED. Peer-reviewed measurement gives ~55% key-field accuracy, positive recall as low as 0.111 (missing ~89% of events) and precision 0.144 at high-frequency nodes. Using it at event level would recreate exactly the call_transcript_gpr.py failure mode the brief warns against. Accepted for AGGREGATE theme intensity only, which is what the literature explicitly endorses.

Querying gdelt-bq.gdeltv2.gkg (the unpartitioned table) — REJECTED on measured cost: 1.88 TB per V2Themes scan, i.e. 188% of the entire monthly BigQuery free tier for one query, and LIMIT does not help. Replaced by gkg_partitioned + _PARTITIONTIME at 379 MB/day.

GDELT raw CSV file ingestion via masterfilelist as the primary path — REJECTED as a false economy. It is genuinely $0 and fully PIT-clean (immutable 15-min files with per-file MD5), but at ~3.7-4.5 MB compressed per 15-min GKG file it is ~360 MB/day compressed and ~130 GB/year to download, decompress and parse on a single Mac. gkg_partitioned delivers the same data inside the free tier with no local storage. Keep the file path as the PIT audit trail / fallback only.

Wikipedia pageviews as a thematic-beneficiary alpha signal — REJECTED for that role. The published effect is index-level (DJIA), contrarian in sign (views up implies returns down), concentrated in the 2008 crisis year (0.89 SD vs 0.19 in 2009/2010), gross of transaction costs by the authors' own admission, and unreplicable on our data because the modern API floor (2015-07-01) does not overlap the study window (2007-2012). Retained only as a low-weight contrarian attention covariate.
Wikipedia EDIT counts as a feature — REJECTED outright on two null results in the founding paper (p>0.9 and p=0.19). Not a judgement call; the evidence is directly against it.

Alpaca news as the historical corpus — REJECTED for the backtest layer. 2015 floor is shallower than GDELT's usable theme window is deep, the archive returns headlines only (hasContent=False measured on 2016 rows), and there is no licence grant for derived works on third-party Benzinga content. Retained as a live forward-collection feed.

POLECAT as a GDELT replacement — CONSIDERED and rejected for this lens despite materially better precision (negative recall 0.904 vs GDELT's 0.144 precision at stressed nodes). Its strength is low false positives at event level, which is not what a theme-intensity series needs; GDELT's high recall is the correct trade for aggregate use, and the literature says so explicitly. Also unverified as a $0 BigQuery-hosted source on the same terms as GDELT.

Treating FRED current-value series as backtest inputs — REJECTED in favour of ALFRED vintages. 1,221 measured vintages for INDPRO back to 1927 make true point-in-time free; using current values would reintroduce the macro-revision lookahead class already recorded in this project's memory.

Monthly rebalancing for the thematic strategy — REJECTED on gate mechanics, not on trading logic: it leaves 8.6 observations per CSCV split at the configured S=16, which cannot yield a trustworthy PBO. Weekly is the minimum viable cadence and is still well inside the cost-negative-turnover boundary the operator set.
open_questions: FRED terms of use could not be retrieved (403 from WebFetch, 000 from curl across three URL variants). The derived-works/commercial clause and the third-party-copyright carve-out for non-government series inside FRED remain UNVERIFIED. Needs a manual browser check before any commercial framing; note the common 'FRED is public domain' claim is only reliably true for US-government-produced series.

No published accuracy audit exists for GDELT's GKG V2Themes field specifically. The ~55% figure measures EVENT records from the CAMEO coder, a different pipeline. Before relying on theme intensity we should run our own small hand-validation (e.g. 200 GKG records across 4 themes) rather than inheriting or dismissing the 55% number — this is a measure-don't-assert case.

Is the Alpha Vantage density discontinuity a backfill artifact or genuine coverage growth? I exhausted the 25/day budget after establishing the >=19x jump between Jan-2025 (53) and Jan-2026 (>=1000). A follow-up day's budget should probe 2026 monthly counts and one mid-cap to confirm. Either way it is PIT-disqualifying, so this is a completeness question, not a decision-blocking one.

Does Alpaca/Benzinga permit derived numeric features (counts, aggregated sentiment) as distinct from redistributing article text? No licence grant appears anywhere in Alpaca's docs. Derived aggregates are lower risk than text redistribution but the question is genuinely unresolved and needs the Alpaca market-data agreement, which requires an authenticated account view.

Are GDELT's BigQuery tables ever retroactively reprocessed? The raw 15-min files are immutable with per-file MD5, but the BQ tables are rebuilt. If BQ history is silently revised, the PIT-clean path is file ingestion rather than BQ, which would materially change the extraction-cost calculus. Testable by hashing a historical BQ partition now and re-hashing in ~30 days.

What is the real-world frequency of cross-sector thematic episodes? I used 2-4/year as a bracket, anchored on the operator's four reference cases in ~6 years. This drives the entire statistical-power conclusion and is currently an assumption, not a measurement. It could be measured directly from the GPR daily series (1985+) by counting threshold exceedances, which would put the episode count on a measured footing across 41 years instead of 11.

Does EDGAR full-text search expose a stable JSON contract? I used efts.sec.gov/LATEST/search-index successfully (HTTP 200, well-formed Elasticsearch response), but 'LATEST' is not a versioned path and SEC does not document this endpoint as a public API. Ingestion should pin behaviour with a contract test, and the 10,000-hit ceiling observed on broad queries needs pagination or date-slicing to enumerate fully.

Does the GPR 2021 methodology break require treating pre-2021 and post-2021 as separate series for gate purposes? GPR_OLD is published alongside, so an overlap-period correlation between the two would answer whether a single continuous series is defensible or whether the break must be modelled as a regime split.

lens: LENS 6 - Lookahead defence and point-in-time discipline for a slow thematic news signal: timestamp protocol, LLM memorization/contamination, purged/combinatorial CV under overlapping weeks-to-months labels, and survivorship in theme->ticker membership. Deliverable = a checkable acceptance protocol + explicit falsifiers.
bottom_line: The binding constraint on a pyfinagent theme backtest is NOT LLM contamination - it is effective sample size and membership provenance. Contamination is measurable and modest when the LLM produces text representations rather than directional per-ticker forecasts (He et al.: ChronoBERT-realtime H-L Sharpe 4.80 vs Llama-3.1-8B 4.90, p=0.630, i.e. ~0.10 Sharpe of leakage), but a 60-120 day overlapping theme label on 4 years of data leaves roughly 10-15 independent label spans, which inflates naive t-stats by ~sqrt(horizon) (~9.5x at 90d) and makes both DSR>=0.95 and a gate-grade PBO structurally unreachable. Three concrete point-in-time defects already exist in the repo and would silently corrupt any backfill: `backend/news/fetcher.py:99` stamps missing publication times with `now()`, `:100` stamps `fetched_at` with `now()` unconditionally (so backfilled rows carry a 2026 ingest clock on 2022 articles), and `backend/backtest/data_ingestion.py:229` writes TODAY's yfinance sector onto every historical fundamentals row, which `historical_data.py:265` feeds to the model as `features["sector"]` - the exact membership-lookahead the theme map would replicate.

key_findings.claim: Gao/Jiang/Yan give the exact detectable-contamination construction. LAP (Lookahead Propensity) is a DATE-ONLY recall query - firm name, ticker, target date, no headline - scored from first-token probabilities: LAP = P_up + P_down (i.e. 1 - P_unknown), with companion directional signal (U-D) = P_up - P_down. The detection test is an interaction regression: r_{i,t+1} = a_i + a_t + phi*LLM_{i,t} + eta*LAP_{i,t+1} + delta*(LAP_{i,t+1} x LLM_{i,t}) + u, firm+date fixed effects, SEs clustered by date (Eq. 7); the earnings-call analogue (Eq. 12) uses CapEx_{i,q+2}, firm+quarter FE, SEs clustered by firm. Positive delta = contamination.
key_findings.numbers: In-sample Bloomberg headlines Jan2012-Dec2023, N=91,357, 1,587 firms: phi = 0.209% (t=12.18); delta = 0.162 (t=3.64); 1 SD of LAP raises the marginal LLM effect by 0.067pp, ~32% of the standalone effect. Validation: theta-hat = 0.264 (t=3.53) for (U-D) alone. Earnings calls 2006Q1-2020Q4, N=106,994, 3,920 firms: phi = 0.547% (t=16.69), delta = 0.512 (t=2.01), 1 SD LAP adds 0.065pp (~12%); validation theta-hat = 0.368 (t=2.13). Post-cutoff 2024 headlines N=7,568: LLM signal SURVIVES at 0.436% (t=6.47) while the interaction VANISHES (t=1.06) and LAP collapses to ~1e-6. Post-cutoff earnings 2023Q3-2024Q1 N=6,744: signal 0.230% (t=3.44), interaction t=1.35, LAP ~1e-7. Bottom-half-LAP subsample: coefficient -0.159, t=-0.33 (statistically zero). Single model tested: Llama-3.3-70B, training cutoff December 2023.

key_findings.claim: He/Lv/Manela/Wu quantify how big the contamination actually is in the architecture pyfinagent would use (text -> embeddings -> separately-fit cross-sectional return model), and the answer is: small and statistically insignificant. This is the single most important number for the design decision, because it says the leakage risk is concentrated in ASKING THE LLM FOR A RETURN, not in using the LLM to represent text.
key_findings.numbers: Dow Jones Newswire, Jan 2008 - Jul 2023, monthly cross-sectional Fama-MacBeth ridge on token-averaged embeddings, decile long-short daily rebalanced. Annualized H-L Sharpe: ChronoBERT-Realtime 4.80; Llama-3.1-8B 4.90 (difference NOT significant, p=0.630); BERT 4.18 (ChronoBERT beats it at 1%, p=0.009); StoriesLM 3.42 (ChronoBERT beats it by ~40%, significant at 1%); FinBERT 3.86. GLUE averages: ChronoBERT_2024 85.54, ChronoBERT_1999 84.71, BERT 84.52, StoriesLM 79.36, FinBERT 76.41. ChronoBERT_1999 = 460B tokens pre-2000, >70 epochs, 149M params; ChronoBERT_2024 = 525B tokens, 26 yearly checkpoints. Paper's own words: "lookahead bias in this context is relatively modest." Implied leakage = 0.10 Sharpe (4.90 - 4.80).

key_findings.claim: NEGATIVE/NULL RESULT that cuts against naive anonymization: Glasserman & Lin found that masking company names IMPROVED in-sample performance, meaning the 'distraction effect' (general company knowledge polluting sentiment reads) is negative and larger than the look-ahead gain. They never isolate a look-ahead magnitude. Out-of-sample the effect is borderline-to-null. Do not adopt entity-masking as a lookahead control on the strength of this paper - it is a confound, not a clean instrument.
key_findings.numbers: GPT-3.5-Turbo, temperature 0, cutoff Sep 2021. In-sample Jan2015-Sep2021: scraped headlines original 25.08 bps/day vs anonymized 30.97 bps/day (t=-1.84, p=0.066); Thomson Reuters original 10.74 vs anonymized 13.84 (t=-2.38, p=0.017). Out-of-sample Oct2021-Dec2022: scraped original 16.32 vs anonymized 11.09 (t=1.20, p=0.23 - NULL); TR original 6.07 vs anonymized 12.23 (t=-1.86, p=0.064 - borderline). Anonymization coverage 100,401/129,431 scraped (77.6%) and 180,237/181,908 TR (99.1%); InDel fuzzy-match threshold 80. Authors: "the distraction effect must be negative and...outweighs the positive gains from look-ahead bias." Explicit caveat: "These strategies are not intended to be feasible... even out-of-sample we are ignoring transaction costs and short-sale constraints."

key_findings.claim: Lopez de Prado's exact purge condition and embargo rule, which is what a theme backtest must encode. A label Y_j = f[[t_j0, t_j1]] overlaps Y_i if ANY of three conditions holds: (1) t_j0 <= t_i0 <= t_j1; (2) t_j0 <= t_i1 <= t_j1; (3) t_i0 <= t_j0 <= t_j1 <= t_i1. Purge = drop every training observation satisfying any of these against the test window. Embargo is a SEPARATE and much smaller control for feature serial correlation, and is needed ONLY AFTER the test set - never before, because training labels ending before the test starts contain only information available at test time.
key_findings.numbers: Embargo length: "A small value h ~= .01T, where T is the number of bars, often suffices to prevent all leakage." CPCV: T observations in N groups, k test groups per split -> C(N,k) splits, and the number of distinct backtest PATHS is phi[N,k] = (k/N)*C(N,k). Worked example N=6, k=2 -> C(6,2)=15 splits, phi[6,2]=5 paths. Stated advantage: "CPCV allows us to derive a distribution of Sharpe ratios, as opposed to a single (likely overfit) Sharpe ratio estimate." DSR: SR* = sqrt(V[{SR_n}]) * ((1-gamma)Z^-1[1 - 1/N] + gamma*Z^-1[1 - (1/N)e^-1]), gamma = 0.5772156649, N = number of independent trials; E[max{x_i}] <= sqrt(2*log[I]).

key_findings.claim: The strongest empirical argument for capturing our OWN ingest timestamps rather than trusting vendor publication times: news-analytics vendors RESTATE their entire history. The Fed paper's identification strategy is built on the fact that RavenPack re-ran all later software versions over the whole archive, so the relevance/sentiment values in today's archive are NOT the values that were on the wire at the time. Any Alpha Vantage NEWS_SENTIMENT archive pull inherits the same hazard: the sentiment scores are the CURRENT model's opinion of a 2022 article, not the 2022 model's.
key_findings.numbers: RavenPack delivers processed content to subscribers "within a third of a second". Share of stock price reaction in the first 5 SECONDS relative to total reaction over 120 seconds is 1.3 percentage points higher for correctly-flagged articles = 10% relative to the mean. Press releases: speed of price response +2.6% vs +0.8% for journalist articles; trade-volume speed +1.4% vs an insignificant +0.2%. HFT share of trading in the first 5s rises 1.8% after RavenPack goes live. Market overreacts to false-positive relevance flags and "quickly corrects after 30 seconds". Press releases are 8% more likely to be the day's first article and 17% more likely to be a new story rather than a reprint. Key provenance sentence: "RavenPack has back-filled the data of all versions to February 2004".

key_findings.claim: DatedGPT gives the cleanest same-model decomposition of the lookahead PREMIUM: hold the model fixed, score the same text with a pre-cutoff vintage vs a post-outcome vintage, and difference. This is directly encodable as our acceptance test - it needs no membership-inference machinery and no proprietary model.
key_findings.numbers: Twelve 1.3B models, cutoffs 2013-2024, ~100B tokens each filtered by FineWeb-Edu crawl date, ~2,000 A100-hours per model. Lookahead-FREE (Table 3 Panel A): DatedGPT-instruct 28.3 bp per SD, Sharpe 3.20, FF5 annualized alpha 0.72 (t=10.09); PIT-4B 29.6 bp, Sharpe 3.37. Lookahead-BIASED (Panel C, 2024-vintage scores): DatedGPT-instruct 33.0 bp, Sharpe 3.65, alpha 1.03 -> delta of +4.7 bp and +0.45 Sharpe. Decomposed lookahead premium (Table 4): DatedGPT-instruct 26.4 bp (t=10.65); PIT-4B 40.1 bp (t=10.98); PIT-4B-FT 12.2 bp (t=3.99); DatedGPT-base 7.7 bp (t=3.13); ChronoGPT premiums INSIGNIFICANT. Knowledge-boundary validation via perplexity reversal at each cutoff. Null result: ChronoGPT-Instruct showed only 5.8 bp return predictability with zero statistical significance.

key_findings.claim: MemGuard-Alpha provides the crossover signature that is the single most diagnostic falsifier for a contaminated signal: in-sample accuracy RISES monotonically with contamination while out-of-sample accuracy FALLS. If a theme backtest shows that pattern across a contamination quintile split, the alpha is memorization. It also shows contamination can be filtered at the signal level for $0 using cross-model disagreement across differing training cutoffs - no retraining required.
key_findings.numbers: 7 LLMs (124M-7B), 50 S&P 100 constituents, 42,800 prompts, 5 MIA methods, Jan 2019 - Jun 2024 (5.5 yr). Accuracy crossover: in-sample 40.8% (Q1 contamination) -> 52.5% (Q5); out-of-sample 47% -> 42%. CMMD-filtered Sharpe 4.11 vs 2.76 unfiltered (+49%). Clean-model signals 14.48 bps average daily return vs 2.13 bps for tainted (7x). MCS Cohen's d = 0.39-1.37 from MIA features alone, d = 18.57 with temporal-proximity features added. Cites Lopez-Lira: GPT-4o recalls exact S&P 500 closing prices with <1% error inside its training window, errors "explode" after cutoff. Cites a systematic review of n=164 financial-LLM papers 2023-2025: no bias type (look-ahead, survivorship, narrative, objective, cost) studied at >28% incidence; practitioner survey n=112, 74% lack ready evaluation tools. Cites FINSABER (KDD 2026): once bias mitigations are applied over a 20-year backtest, LLM alpha differences VANISH.

key_findings.claim: Look-Ahead-Bench reports the largest headline contamination numbers in the literature - and simultaneously refutes its own metric. Alpha decay between an in-sample and out-of-sample window is NOT a clean lookahead measure, because the paper's own RANDOM NOISE control and a mean-reversion baseline decayed by comparable double digits with zero memorization possible. Do NOT adopt raw alpha-decay as our acceptance criterion.
key_findings.numbers: P1 (in-sample) Apr-Sep 2021, P2 (OOS) Jul-Dec 2024, 5 tickers (AAPL/MSFT/GOOGL/NVDA/TSLA), monthly rebalance. Alpha decay in pp: Llama-3.1-8B -17.23, Llama-3.1-70B -15.25, DeepSeek 3.2 -21.77; Pitinf-Small +0.31, Medium +0.85, Large +1.30. BUT the baselines: Momentum(3M) -2.21, Equal Weight -2.78, MA Crossover +9.94, Mean Reversion -10.78, and RANDOM NOISE control -10.30. So a strategy with literally no information decayed 10.30pp. DeepSeek's P1 alpha was +20.73pp and P2 -1.04pp. Author's own limitations: universe restricted to 5 large-cap US tech; recommends ">=20-30 stocks across multiple sectors" and "4+ periods". The winning 'Pitinf' family is PROPRIETARY, from a vendor (PiT-Inference, 2026) - unreproducible and a conflict-of-interest risk.

key_findings.claim: Empirically, naive (unpurged) CV on serially-correlated data with overlapping labels does not merely inflate results - it manufactures R-squared out of pure noise, and purging drives the same fit BELOW a predict-the-mean baseline. === PART A: THREE CLOCKS AND THE EMBARGO ===

A1. Persist three distinct timestamps per article, never two: t_pub (publisher's stated time, vendor-supplied, RESTATABLE), t_ingest (when OUR process first received the row, self-captured, immutable), t_act (the first exchange session whose OPEN we could have transacted at). Add a fourth non-null column `provenance` in {live, backfill}. CHECK: schema of news_articles contains published_at, fetched_at, provenance, and effective_trade_date, all REQUIRED. MUTATION: dropping provenance must fail the schema assertion.

A2. FIX `backend/news/fetcher.py:99` - a missing publication timestamp must yield None and route the article to a quarantine counter, never `_now_iso()`. FIX `:100` - `fetched_at` must be `now()` ONLY when provenance=live; for provenance=backfill it must be NULL (there was no ingest event). CHECK: a fixture RawArticle with no published_at must produce a row with published_at=None and increment a `dropped_no_pubtime` counter. MUTATION: restoring the `or _now_iso()` fallback must fail that fixture.

A3. THE DEFENSIBLE EMBARGO IS ONE FULL SESSION, ENTERING AT THE NEXT OPEN. Rule: effective_trade_date = next_trading_day(D) where D = the exchange-local calendar date of t_pub if t_pub < 16:00 ET, else that date + 1. Position is entered at effective_trade_date's OPEN, never the publication day's close. Justification chain, not arbitrary conservatism: (i) the microstructure race is over in ~120 seconds (von Beschwitz et al.: reaction concentrated in the first 5s, false-positive corrections complete within 30s, RavenPack delivery in 1/3 second) - a daily-cycle retail system on a $0 rail has already conceded that window and must not model any part of it; (ii) the operator's channel is explicitly weeks-to-months, so a one-session embargo costs a negligible fraction of the holding period; (iii) it is the only rule that is identical for live and backfilled rows, which is what makes the backtest and the live path comparable at all. DO NOT use a same-day-close entry and DO NOT use an intraday embargo - both require a timestamp precision we cannot verify on backfilled vendor data. CHECK: assert min(effective_trade_date - t_pub_date) >= 1 trading day over the entire corpus, and assert the entry price used equals the OPEN. MUTATION: setting the embargo to 0 days must make the assertion fail.

A4. TREAT ALL VENDOR SENTIMENT SCORES AS RESTATED. The Fed paper's whole identification strategy rests on RavenPack having 'back-filled the data of all versions to February 2004'. Alpha Vantage NEWS_SENTIMENT's relevance_score / ticker_sentiment_score on a 2022 article is the CURRENT scorer's opinion, not the 2022 scorer's - it is a lookahead-contaminated field by construction. RULE: vendor sentiment scores may be used as a FEATURE only if the same restatement hazard is disclosed in the results, and may NEVER be used as the label or as the theme-assignment key. Prefer deriving our own score from the article TEXT (which is not restated) with a dated model. CHECK: grep the feature list for any vendor-supplied sentiment column and require a matching disclosure line in experiment_results.md.

=== PART B: LLM CONTAMINATION ===

B1. ARCHITECTURAL RULE (largest single risk reduction, zero cost). The LLM must never be asked 'will TICKER go up'. It may only emit (a) a theme taxonomy, (b) a theme->beneficiary mapping with cited evidence URLs, or (c) a text representation. Return prediction must be done by a separately-fit, purged, point-in-time statistical model on top. Evidence: this is exactly the He et al. architecture where measured contamination was 0.10 Sharpe with p=0.630; whereas the direct-forecast setups (Gao et al., Look-Ahead-Bench, MemGuard) are where contamination bites. This also satisfies the cycle-level-not-per-ticker LLM cost constraint.

B2. RUN THE LAP TEST, IT IS CHEAP AND EXACT. Implement Gao et al. Eq.7 verbatim: r_{i,t+1} = a_i + a_t + phi*LLM_{i,t} + eta*LAP_{i,t+1} + delta*(LAP x LLM) + u, firm and date fixed effects, SEs clustered by date. LAP = P_up + P_down from a DATE-ONLY recall prompt ('On {date}, did the closing stock price of {company} ({ticker}) go up or down compared to the previous trading day? Answer based only on what you recall... Respond with exactly one word: up, down, or unknown'), read off first-token probabilities. PASS CONDITION: delta is not significant at 5% (their contaminated in-sample benchmark was delta=0.162, t=3.64; their clean post-cutoff benchmark was t=1.06). NOTE THE $0 CONSTRAINT: first-token logprobs are required, so this test runs on a local open-weights model (Llama-class), not on the Gemini/Claude API rail - budget it as a one-off research run, not a per-cycle cost.

B3. RUN THE VINTAGE-DIFFERENCE TEST (the DatedGPT decomposition) - it needs no logprobs and no MIA machinery. Score the SAME article text twice: once with a model whose cutoff precedes the article, once with the current model. The difference is the lookahead premium. PASS CONDITION: premium is statistically insignificant, or is disclosed with its exact magnitude and the strategy is evaluated on the pre-cutoff-vintage score only. Reference magnitudes: DatedGPT-instruct 26.4 bp (t=10.65), PIT-4B 40.1 bp (t=10.98), Sharpe delta +0.45.

B4. RUN THE CONTAMINATION-QUINTILE CROSSOVER TEST (MemGuard-Alpha's signature). Split signals into contamination quintiles and plot in-sample vs out-of-sample directional accuracy. FALSIFIER: if in-sample accuracy RISES with contamination while out-of-sample accuracy FALLS (their measured 40.8%->52.5% vs 47%->42%), the alpha is memorization and the strategy is dead. This is the single most diagnostic cheap test.

B5. DO NOT use entity anonymization as the control (Glasserman & Lin: it made in-sample results BETTER; Wu et al. via MemGuard: information loss can exceed the bias). DO NOT use raw alpha-decay as the criterion (Look-Ahead-Bench's own random-noise control decayed -10.30pp). If alpha decay is reported at all, it must be reported alongside a zero-information control run over the identical windows.

=== PART C: PURGING, EMBARGO, AND THE OVERLAPPING-LABEL PROBLEM (THE BINDING CONSTRAINT) ===

C1. PURGE ON THE THEME'S OWN HORIZON, NOT holding_days. The existing purge (`backtest_engine.py:579-591`, horizon = 1.5*holding_days at :665) is correctly shaped but the horizon constant is wrong for a theme signal: a theme's label span is the theme's persistence (weeks-to-months), which is a property of the THEME, not of the trader's exit rule. Add an explicit `theme_label_horizon_days` and purge on max(1.5*holding_days, theme_label_horizon_days). CHECK: `_label_overlaps_test` called with the theme horizon must purge strictly MORE samples than with the holding horizon; assert the purged count is non-zero and strictly greater. MUTATION: setting theme_label_horizon_days=0 must fail.

C2. KEEP THE 5-DAY EMBARGO AS IS AND DO NOT CONFLATE IT WITH THE PURGE. Lopez de Prado is explicit: the embargo handles FEATURE serial correlation, applies ONLY AFTER the test set, and 'a small value h ~= .01T... often suffices'. With ~1000 trading days, .01T = 10 days, so the current default of 5 (`settings.py:255`) is at the low end - raise to 10 for a theme signal and cite .01T. The 60-120 day exposure is the PURGE's job, not the embargo's.

C3. REPORT THE EFFECTIVE SAMPLE SIZE AND CORRECT EVERY t-STAT FOR IT. THIS IS THE GATE MOST LIKELY TO KILL THE PROJECT AND IT MUST BE FACED FIRST. With a 90-day overlapping label and daily sampling, N calendar observations carry roughly N/90 independent label spans; a naive t-stat is inflated by ~sqrt(90) ~= 9.5x. On 4 years (~1000 trading days) that is ~11 independent spans. The current biweekly training sampler (`backtest_engine.py:651-657`) with horizon 1.5*90=135d gives each sample ~9-10 overlapping neighbours. REQUIRED: report `n_independent = span_days / theme_label_horizon_days` alongside every headline metric, and compute all t-stats either on NON-OVERLAPPING spans or with Newey-West lag >= theme_label_horizon_days. FALSIFIER: any theme result whose significance survives only on the overlapping series is not evidence. Also verify the existing uniqueness/sample-weighting path uses the SAME 1.5x horizon (Lopez de Prado Pitfall #7).

C4. USE CPCV, NOT WALK-FORWARD, AND COMPUTE THE PATH COUNT. `gate.py::cpcv_folds` currently returns all C(n,k) splits and never computes phi[N,k] = (k/N)*C(N,k), which is the number of distinct backtest PATHS and therefore the effective N for the DSR trial-count and the PBO. Add phi. Worked target: to reach ~100+ paths (the R reference N for PBO), N=10,k=5 gives phi=(5/10)*252=126. CRITICAL CONSEQUENCE, STATE IT IN THE CONTRACT: N=10 groups on ~11 independent label spans is degenerate. A single-time-series theme backtest on <10 years CANNOT produce a gate-grade PBO. The only escapes are (a) extend history (Alpha Vantage archive reaches 2022-02-24 -> ~4.4 years, NOT enough), or (b) evaluate CROSS-SECTIONALLY - many themes x many beneficiary names - so the independent-observation count comes from theme x name pairs rather than from calendar time. Option (b) is the only $0-compatible route and should be the design's spine. CHECK: assert pbo_n_trials >= 10 (already enforced at gate.py:30) AND assert phi[N,k] >= pbo_n_trials AND assert n_independent >= phi[N,k]. MUTATION: shrinking the sample must fail the third assertion.

C5. PURGE INSIDE EVERY CPCV FOLD, NOT JUST ON THE WALK-FORWARD PATH. CPCV test groups are non-contiguous, so a training sample can sit between two test groups and overlap BOTH. Apply the three Lopez de Prado conditions against EVERY test group in the fold, and embargo after EACH contiguous test block. CHECK: construct a fixture where a sample's label spans a gap between two test groups; it must be purged. MUTATION: purging against only the first test group must fail that fixture. Run the leakage mutation from the purged-CV literature: with purging DISABLED on pure-noise features the metric must blow UP (their benchmark: R^2 0.83-0.91 on noise unpurged vs below predict-the-mean purged). A purge whose removal does not change the number is not doing anything.

=== PART D: THEME-MEMBERSHIP SURVIVORSHIP (THE SUBTLEST LEAK) ===

D1. THE CORE PROBLEM, STATED PLAINLY: 'AI rush -> memory + datacenter names' is a list we know BECAUSE those names went up. An LLM in 2026 asked to name AI beneficiaries returns the WINNERS. Applying that list to 2023 is look-ahead and survivorship simultaneously, and it is strictly worse than index-membership bias because a theme member list is far more outcome-correlated than an index. Reference magnitudes for the weaker index version: current-constituent S&P backtests overstate CAGR ~3.7%; an S&P 100 trend example falls 11.7% -> 6.1%.

D2. FIX THE EXISTING INSTANCE FIRST. `data_ingestion.py:229/:274` stamps TODAY's yfinance sector onto every historical fundamentals row and `historical_data.py:265` feeds it to the model. This is the same bug class, already live, already in `_NUMERIC_FEATURES`-adjacent territory, and already used for peer grouping (`peer_leadlag_screen.py:75-82`). Queue it as its own masterplan step (per feedback_queue_discovered_defects_in_masterplan) - do not fold it into the theme work.

D3. MAKE MEMBERSHIP BITEMPORAL. Table shape: (theme_id, ticker, valid_from, valid_to, decided_at, decided_by_model, model_cutoff, evidence_urls[], evidence_pub_dates[]). `decided_at` is the point-in-time key; the backtest reads WHERE decided_at <= as_of_date. HARD RULE: every evidence_pub_date must be strictly < decided_at, and model_cutoff must be <= decided_at. CHECK: assert max(evidence_pub_dates) < decided_at for every row, and assert no backtest query ever reads a row with decided_at > as_of. MUTATION: inserting one row with a future evidence URL must fail the assertion.

D4. INCLUDE THE LOSERS AND THE DEAD. The membership snapshot at time T must contain every name the theme logic would have selected at T, including names that were later delisted, acquired, or dropped out of the theme. A theme member list that only contains names still alive in 2026 is survivorship-biased by construction. CHECK: assert the historical membership set contains at least one ticker absent from the current universe; if it contains zero, the snapshot is not point-in-time.

D5. RECONSTRUCT MEMBERSHIP FROM DATED TEXT, NOT FROM MODEL RECALL. The only defensible construction is: at as_of date T, run the mapper over articles with t_pub < T ONLY, and let it emit beneficiaries. Never prompt 'who benefited from the AI buildout'. This also makes D3's assertion mechanically satisfiable.

=== PART E: WHAT WOULD FALSIFY A THEME BACKTEST (report these as the pre-registered kill conditions) ===

F1. The contamination crossover appears: in-sample accuracy rises with contamination quintile while out-of-sample accuracy falls.
F2. delta in the LAP interaction regression is significant at 5% on the evaluation sample.
F3. The vintage-difference lookahead premium is significant AND the strategy's edge is smaller than that premium.
F4. n_independent (span_days / theme_label_horizon_days) is below the PBO trial floor, or phi[N,k] < 10 - the result is directional, never gate-grade.
F5. Disabling the purge does not change the headline metric - proof the purge is a no-op guard.
F6. The historical membership snapshot contains zero tickers that are absent from today's universe - proof it is not point-in-time.
F7. Any evidence URL backing a membership decision has t_pub >= decided_at.
F8. Performance collapses when entry moves from the publication-day close to the next-day open - the edge lived inside the embargo we cannot actually capture.
F9. A zero-information control (random weights) run over the identical windows shows comparable degradation - the 'decay' is regime, not skill.
F10. After costs, the surviving edge does not clear the incumbent OOS - the standing promotion gate, unchanged.

5. Only then run B2/B3/B4. They are cheap and they are the tests that decide whether the LLM leg is admissible at all.

This is a genuine gap in the literature.

The LAP test (B2) requires first-token logprobs, which the Gemini/Claude API rail does not expose in the shape Gao et al. use. Whether a local open-weights model of adequate quality fits the measured 13.7/16GB memory ceiling (per project_local_llm_verdict) is unresolved; if not, B2 is not executable and B3 (the vintage-difference test, which needs no logprobs) must carry the whole contamination gate alone.

lens: LENS 7 — NEGATIVE EVIDENCE (adversarial case against building a news-driven cross-sector thematic signal)
bottom_line: The strongest single argument is arithmetic, not opinion: the promotion gate is already unreachable on the available data. With Alpha Vantage news starting 2022-02-24, a weeks-to-months signal has at most ~53 monthly observations; my own PSR/DSR computation says DSR>=0.95 then requires an annualised Sharpe of ~1.97 after only 45 trials (~2.37 if fat-tailed) — while every value-weighted, low-turnover, large-cap analog in the literature delivers 0.67–1.33, and the direct professional implementation of "buy the beneficiaries of a theme when media sentiment is high" has a MEASURED alpha of about -6%/yr. Worse, the in-sample evidence would be uninterpretable anyway: frontier LLMs have memorised all four of the operator's reference cases, and prompt-based "pretend you don't know" mitigations are measured to fail (97.6% vs 98.0% accuracy with and without an artificial cutoff instruction).

key_findings.claim: The documented news-return effect lives in a 1-4 day window, is a SMALL-CAP effect, and its net-of-cost optimum requires ~46% DAILY turnover — i.e. it exists only in exactly the fast, high-turnover, small-cap channel the operator has ruled out of scope. There is no documented weeks-to-months, large-cap, low-turnover news alpha to harvest.
key_findings.numbers: RavenPack and Loughran-McDonald signals "fully incorporated into prices within two days"; SESTM requires four days. Equal-weighted L/S annualised Sharpe 4.29 vs value-weighted 1.33 (a 3.2x small-cap concentration). Daily turnover 94% EW / 90% VW. With 10bps daily cost, net Sharpe peaks at 2.30 at gamma=0.5 = 46% average daily turnover; at gamma=0.1 (8% turnover) net Sharpe falls to 1.17. One-day L/S return: SESTM 33bps, RavenPack 18bps, LM dictionary 12bps.

key_findings.claim: The professional, well-capitalised implementation of this exact idea — identify a theme from media, launch a basket of its beneficiaries — has a measured NEGATIVE alpha, and the subset selected on HIGH MEDIA SENTIMENT is the worst-performing subset. High media sentiment on a theme is empirically a negative-alpha selector, which is precisely the selection rule a news-driven theme detector implements.
key_findings.numbers: Specialized/thematic ETFs: risk-adjusted return -3.1%/yr after fees; about -6% annually in the first five years after inception; about -30% cumulative risk-adjusted over five years. FFC4 alpha -3.24%/yr vs -0.24%/yr for broad-based; fee gap only 0.13%/yr (an order of magnitude too small to explain it). Split on pre-launch returns AND media sentiment: high-sentiment ETFs deliver monthly FFC4 alpha of -0.53% (approx -6.4%/yr) vs -0.20%/month for low-sentiment. Sample 2000-2019. Named example themes include "trade war, cannabis, vegan products, work from home, and COVID-19 vaccines."

key_findings.claim: The intellectual foundation of theme->second-order-beneficiary (Cohen-Frazzini economic-link predictability) has DECAYED to statistical insignificance in the modern sample, and specifically in the value-weighted (large-cap) implementation pyfinagent would use.
key_findings.numbers: Full sample 1978-2018: EW L/S 1.22%/mo (t=5.17), FF5+UMD alpha 1.14% (t=4.55); VW 1.06%/mo (t=3.34), alpha 0.91% (t=2.69). Sub-period split: EW L/S 1.52%/mo (1978-2004) -> 0.62%/mo (2005-2018), a 59% decline; VW 1.30% -> 0.62%, a 52% decline. In 2005-2018 the EW t=2.12 (marginal) and the VW t=1.54 — NOT significant. Authors: "Returns of value-weighted long-short portfolios, formed on customer momentum, are not significantly different from zero." Also: customer momentum at 6-1 and 12-1 lags "is captured by price momentum" — only the 1-month lag has independent power.

key_findings.claim: LLM-generated in-sample evidence for a theme->beneficiary map is UNFALSIFIABLE, because the model has memorised the outcomes. Prompt-based mitigations ('ignore what you know after date X') are measured to fail outright. The operator's four reference cases are the four most-documented macro narratives in every frontier model's training corpus.
key_findings.numbers: S&P 500 directional accuracy 80.58% pre-cutoff -> 45.70% post-cutoff (worse than a coin flip); MAPE 0.61% -> 16.87%. Headline dating: year-identification accuracy 98.45% -> 28.81%; exact-date 47.03% -> 7.86%; mean absolute error 414.54 days post-cutoff. META recall: MAPE 0.37%, directional accuracy 99.26%. GDP-growth MAE 0.15% -> 0.95%, threshold accuracy 96% -> 40%. FAKE-CUTOFF TEST: 97.6% threshold accuracy before an artificial 2010 cutoff and 98.0% after, DESPITE explicit instructions to ignore post-2010 data. Authors: "any observed forecast is consistent with two contradictory explanations (genuine analytical skill or simple recall of memorized information)."

key_findings.claim: When an LLM stock-selection signal is moved outside its training window, the alpha does not decay — it vanishes and flips sign. A related paper shows the LLM news signal's predictive power is concentrated exactly at high-'lookahead-propensity' firm-dates and becomes statistically insignificant post-cutoff.
key_findings.numbers: Look-Ahead-Bench (Benhenda 2026): DeepSeek 3.2 stock-selection strategy +20.73% annualised alpha in-sample (Apr-Sep 2021, inside training data) -> -1.04% out-of-sample (Jul-Dec 2024, after cutoff); decay of -21.77 percentage points. Lookahead-Propensity paper: LLM news signal predicts "0.21% higher next-day return" in-sample, "amplified at high LAP" firm-dates; post-cutoff (2024) the interaction "becomes statistically insignificant". Earnings-call application: 0.547pp capex effect, interaction diminishes post-cutoff.

key_findings.claim: LLMs asked to construct firm-relationship graphs produce confident, plausible, WRONG links — and accuracy collapses precisely in the low-visibility regime, which is by definition where second-order beneficiaries live. Multi-source consensus checking does not fix it.
key_findings.numbers: Claude Opus 4.6 standalone: graph F1 0.63, entity F1 0.67, relation F1 0.57 (vs Helicase 0.85/0.87/0.83). Accuracy by quadrant: Claude Opus 80% on single-hop HIGH-visibility (Q1) but only 55% on single-hop LOW-visibility (Q3); DeepSeek-V3.2 40%/15%; Qwen3-235B 30%/5%. Paper documents Claude Opus "did not reliably connect those ingredients to upstream suppliers" and returned "unsupported or incorrect supplier names." Authors' caveat: "when a single erroneous claim is recycled across analyst reports, trade press, and aggregator sites, the multiplicative accumulation update will assign that claim high confidence"; the system remains "vulnerable to adversarial information attacks."

key_findings.claim: The base rate for this class of claim surviving replication is poor, and the honest significance hurdle is t>~2.8-3.5, not 1.96. Cohen-Frazzini customer momentum is named explicitly among the anomalies whose replicated magnitudes are much smaller than published.
key_findings.numbers: Hou-Xue-Zhang: 452 anomalies; with NYSE breakpoints + value-weighting, 65% fail |t|>=1.96, and 82% fail the multiple-test hurdle |t|>=2.78; 102 of 106 (96%) trading-frictions anomalies fail. Applying Benjamini-Hochberg-Yekutieli to their own 452 yields |t| cutoffs of 3.47 (5%) and 4.27 (1%). Microcaps are only 3.2% of aggregate market cap yet "can account for more than 60% of the stocks in extreme deciles" under NYSE-Amex-NASDAQ breakpoints. Harvey-Liu-Zhu: 316 factors documented; recommended hurdle t>3.0; Bonferroni cutoff rises 1.96 -> 3.78 by 2012 -> 4.00 by 2032; Holm 3.64; BHY 3.39 (1%) / 2.78 (5%); "most claimed research findings in financial economics are likely false."

key_findings.claim: Post-publication decay is LARGEST for exactly pyfinagent's universe: large, liquid, dividend-paying, low-idiosyncratic-risk stocks. The S&P 500 is the worst place to harvest a newly-legible predictor.
key_findings.numbers: Working-paper version (82 characteristics): out-of-sample decay from statistical bias ~10%, "not statistically different from zero" (t=-1.40 on the 78%-of-in-sample OOS pre-publication mean); post-publication decay ~35% (t=-4.91), robust across specifications (37%, 42%, 34%). Published JF version (97 predictors): 26% lower out-of-sample, 58% lower post-publication, implying ~32% attributable to publication-informed trading. "the post-publication return decline is greater for anomaly portfolios that consist of stocks that are large, liquid, have high dividend yields, and have low idiosyncratic risk."

key_findings.claim: MY OWN COMPUTATION against the project's actual gate: the maximum honest sample cannot support a DSR>=0.95 verdict at any plausible effect size. This is the decisive constraint and it is not a matter of engineering effort.
key_findings.numbers: Alpha Vantage news from 2022-02-24 -> ~53 monthly observations at a weeks-to-months horizon. Bailey et al: "if only five years of daily stock market data are available as a backtest, then no more than 45 variations of a strategy should be tried on this data, or the resulting strategy will be overfit, in the specific sense that the strategy's Sharpe Ratio is likely to be 1.0 or greater just by chance (even though the true SR may be zero or negative)"; two years of daily data supports at most seven variations. My PSR/DSR calculation (T=53 monthly obs, trial-Sharpe dispersion 0.5 annualised): DSR>=0.95 requires annualised Sharpe 1.07 at N=1 trial, 1.62 at N=10, 1.97 at N=45, 2.13 at N=100, 2.52 at N=1000. With skew=-1.0 and kurtosis=8 (a realistic fat-tailed thematic L/S): 1.93 at N=10, 2.37 at N=45, 2.56 at N=100. Separately, CSCV/PBO at the risk-MCP default S=16 over 53 rows leaves ~3 observations per split — the PBO estimate would be noise.

key_findings.claim: Crowding is directly observable in the news-sentiment literature itself: the commercially-distributed signal flattened as institutional adoption grew, while the proprietary unpublished one did not. Free, legible news is the most-crowded end of that spectrum and produces the weakest measured signal.
key_findings.numbers: "Following 2008, and especially in mid 2014, the slope of the RavenPack strategy noticeably flattens... anecdotes from the asset management industry suggest that subscriptions to RavenPack by financial institutions grew rapidly over this time period. In contrast, the slope of SESTM is generally stable during our test [period]." Signal strength ordering: proprietary SESTM 33bps > commercial RavenPack 18bps > free LM dictionary 12bps one-day L/S return. Separately, momentum's Sharpe fell from ~1.5 in the mid-1990s to ~0.25 today, with Pearson rho = -0.63 (p<0.001) between cumulative decay residuals and factor ETF volume (2013-2024).

key_findings.claim: The choice of sentiment model — a free parameter with no theory to pin it down — FLIPS THE SIGN of the alpha. Two of three sentiment specifications produced negative alpha and underperformed buy-and-hold; the headline Sharpe of 3.98 is one arbitrary architecture out of three over a 28-month COVID window with no transaction costs reported.
key_findings.numbers: Jan 1 2020 - Apr 30 2022. Alpha: RoBERTa+Transfs +23.67%, FinBERT -1.73%, DualGCN -11.47%. Cumulative return: Buy&Hold 26.96%, FinBERT 25.23%, DualGCN 15.49% (both sentiment classifiers BELOW the passive baseline). Sharpe: Buy&Hold 0.38, DualGCN 1.92, FinBERT 2.31, RoBERTa+Transfs 3.98. Buy&Hold led 2021 (18.24% vs 10.73%). No transaction-cost line in the metrics table.

key_findings.claim: The nearest published analog to the proposed system is a weak, non-peer-reviewed, single-author preprint whose signal is an uninterpretable 5th principal component with a t-stat BELOW the honest multiple-testing hurdle, and whose own authors say scaling it requires PAID vendor data.
key_findings.numbers: 255 S&P 500 firms, Jan 2011-Dec 2025, 2,365 10-K filings, 24,723 firm-months, 174 monthly observations. Signal = net_pc_5, Newey-West t = -2.64 (NEGATIVE sign; long the BOTTOM quintile). Annualised return 10.9%, vol 12.6%, gross Sharpe 0.86, max drawdown -16.9%; net Sharpe 0.67 after 20bps round-trip. FF5 alpha 7.27%/yr, t=2.30 — below Harvey-Liu-Zhu's 3.0 and below Hou-Xue-Zhang's 2.78. Direct (non-network) LLM portfolio: gross Sharpe 0.56, net 0.34. FF5 spanning R-squared only 0.185. Stated limitations: KG is "manually curated supply chain relationships among a subset of S&P 500 constituents", future work "should exploit commercial data sources such as FactSet Supply Chain or Bloomberg SPLC"; no book-to-market/profitability/investment controls because of "data access constraints". Uses annual 10-K MD&A, NOT news.

key_findings.claim: Thematic funds' survival-AND-success base rate over horizons matching a weeks-to-months holding discipline compounded over years is catastrophic, and survivorship bias hides most of it.
key_findings.numbers: Global thematic funds as of 2021-12-31: over the trailing 15 years, "more than three fourths of thematic funds globally have shuttered and just one in 10 survived and outperformed" the Morningstar Global Markets Index; 5-year success rate 39%; 3-year success rate just over 50%. US: "over the 10 years through the end of 2021, nearly 60% of U.S. thematic funds shuttered, and just 22% both survived and outperformed." Europe 15-year success rate 9%. In 2021 alone, "more than two thirds of thematic funds underperformed the Morningstar Global Markets Index."

key_findings.claim: The theme-timing penalty is measured and is ~10x worse for thematic than for ordinary equity funds — the loss comes from acting on a theme once it is legible, which is mechanically what a news-driven theme detector does.
key_findings.numbers: Five years to 2023-06-30: thematic funds' average total return 7.3% annualised, investor (asset-weighted) return only 2.4% — a 4.9 percentage-point annual gap, "more than two thirds of total returns" lost to timing. Comparison: 0.5% gap for ALL equity funds over the same period. Focused themes (Technology, Physical World) had gaps "over 500 basis points" vs 111bps for Broad Thematic funds. ETF gaps ran ~500-600bps wider than mutual funds on the same theme (over 9% vs almost 4% for energy-transition).

key_findings.claim: HONEST COUNTER-EVIDENCE (must be weighed): Chen and Zimmermann argue the replication crisis in cross-sectional asset pricing is overstated. I report this because it is the strongest rebuttal to my base-rate argument — but note its scope does not transfer: it covers numeric CRSP/Compustat characteristics with multi-decade samples, not 4-year LLM-generated text mappings.
key_findings.numbers: For the 161 characteristics clearly significant in the original papers, 98% of long-short portfolios reproduce t-stats above 1.96. Publication-bias-adjusted returns are only 12.3% smaller than in-sample returns (standard error 1.7 percentage points). Their four stylised facts: almost all findings replicate, predictability persists out-of-sample, empirical t-stats are much larger than 2.0, and predictors are weakly correlated.

key_findings.claim: HONEST COUNTER-EVIDENCE: cross-industry gradual information diffusion IS a real documented effect at a horizon of up to two months — the one result that genuinely supports the operator's thesis. But its own literature states the effect shrinks precisely where analyst coverage and institutional ownership are highest, i.e. the S&P 500.
key_findings.numbers: Hong-Torous-Valkanov: industries including retail, services, commercial real estate, metal and petroleum lead the market by up to two months. Mitigating finding: "the magnitude of return cross-predictability declines with the number of informed investors in the market as proxied by the level of analyst coverage and institutional ownership"; cross-predictability "fades as common institutional ownership emerges."

key_findings.claim: The magnitude and even the SIGN of LLM-sentiment bias is not predictable a priori, so a project cannot bound its own contamination with a simple correction term. Anonymising company names to remove look-ahead bias made in-sample performance BETTER, not worse.
key_findings.numbers: In-sample: scraped headlines original 25.08 bps/day vs name-replaced 30.97 bps/day (difference 5.89 bps/day, t=-1.84, p=0.066); Thomson Reuters original 10.74 vs replaced 13.84 bps/day (t=-2.38, p=0.017). Out-of-sample (Oct 2021-Dec 2022): scraped original 16.32 vs replaced 11.09 (t=1.20, p=0.23, insignificant); Reuters original 6.07 vs replaced 12.23 (t=-1.86, p=0.064). Misclassification cost: -242bps in-sample / -289bps OOS when the original response is wrong and the replaced is neutral. Authors: "the distraction effect must be negative" and outweighs the look-ahead benefit. Caveat: "Strategies ignore transaction costs and short-sale constraints", equal-weighted DAILY rebalancing.

negative_or_null_results: Cohen-Frazzini customer momentum is NOT significant value-weighted in 2005-2018: 0.62%/month, t=1.54. Equal-weighted t=2.12 is marginal and would fail the Hou-Xue-Zhang multiple-testing hurdle of 2.78. The cross-firm-link mechanism the whole project rests on is a dead effect in the modern large-cap sample.

65% of 452 published anomalies fail |t|>=1.96 with NYSE breakpoints and value-weighting; 82% fail at |t|>=2.78; 96% of the trading-frictions category fails. Applying BHY to that library gives cutoffs of 3.47/4.27.

McLean-Pontiff working-paper version: the pure out-of-sample (pre-publication) decay of ~10% is "not statistically different from zero" (t=-1.40). The real decay is post-publication (~35%, t=-4.91) and it is largest in large/liquid/dividend-paying/low-idio-vol stocks — pyfinagent's universe.

Two of three sentiment-model specifications produced NEGATIVE alpha (-11.47% DualGCN, -1.73% FinBERT) and BOTH underperformed passive buy-and-hold cumulatively (15.49% and 25.23% vs 26.96%) over Jan 2020-Apr 2022.
Look-Ahead-Bench: DeepSeek 3.2 LLM stock-selection alpha went from +20.73% annualised in-sample to -1.04% out-of-sample. The alpha did not decay; it disappeared.
LLM post-cutoff S&P 500 directional accuracy is 45.70% — worse than random. Pre-cutoff it is 80.58%.
Prompt-based look-ahead mitigation FAILS: 97.6% vs 98.0% threshold accuracy with and without an explicit instruction to ignore post-2010 data. There is no prompt that makes a memorising model forget.

Crowding-based factor timing is itself a null: the crowding-timed strategy earned Sharpe 0.22 versus 0.39 for a plain factor-momentum benchmark and 0.17 equal-weight (2017-2025). "crowding-based factor selection fails to generate alpha."

Glasserman-Lin: removing look-ahead bias by anonymising company names IMPROVED in-sample returns (30.97 vs 25.08 bps/day). The contamination does not have a predictable sign, so it cannot be corrected for with an adjustment factor.

Broad-based ETF performance is "slightly negative, though statistically indistinguishable from zero" while specialized/thematic ETFs are significantly negative — the underperformance is specific to thematic concentration, not to the ETF wrapper.

Customer momentum at 6-1 and 12-1 month lags "is captured by price momentum" — at the operator's target horizon (weeks-to-months), the cross-firm signal is subsumed by ordinary momentum, which pyfinagent already has four of in _NUMERIC_FEATURES.
recommendation_for_pyfinagent: DO NOT build the LLM theme->beneficiary mapper as an alpha source. Not "build it carefully" — do not build it, because it cannot clear DSR>=0.95 / PBO<=0.5 on the available sample and that is arithmetic (see key finding 9), and because any in-sample support it produces would be memorisation, not foresight. Concretely: (1) If the operator insists on a decisive test rather than a decision, run ONE pre-registered kill-test and nothing more, because a 53-month sample supports N~1-10 trials, not a search. Create the two missing BQ tables (news_articles, news_sentiment — schemas already exist at scripts/migrations/add_news_sentiment_schema.py:64-107), backfill Alpha Vantage NEWS_SENTIMENT ticker relevance+sentiment for the S&P 500 from 2022-02-24, add exactly ONE feature to backend/backtest/backtest_engine.py:50 _NUMERIC_FEATURES (trailing-21d relevance-weighted sentiment), and run the existing gate. (2) Pre-register the kill criterion IN WRITING BEFORE looking: value-weighted only (the entire documented effect is a small-cap effect — EW Sharpe 4.29 vs VW 1.33), FF5-alpha t must exceed 2.78 not 1.96, turnover capped at <=12%/month, and net of costs. If it misses, the step closes as FAIL and the idea is retired — no second spec, no second horizon, no "let's try a different sentiment model" (that free parameter flipped the sign of alpha from -11.47% to +23.67% in the CORIA study). (3) NEVER let an LLM propose a theme->beneficiary mapping over any window inside its training data. If a mapping is used at all, freeze it ex ante and score it FORWARD-ONLY in paper trading; log the signal daily starting now and revisit in ~3 years when there is an honest OOS sample. That forward log costs ~$0 and is the only clean evidence path available. (4) If anything survives, ship it scoped as a RISK FILTER (veto / size-down), exactly the call already made in backend/services/call_transcript_gpr.py, not as an alpha overlay — a filter does not have to clear the alpha gate. (5) Higher-value use of the same effort: pyfinagent already runs news_screen LIVE (NEWS_SCREEN_ENABLED=true) while the backtest engine has ZERO news features among its 37 — so news already moves live trades and is un-gate-able today. Closing THAT hole (persist the corpus, backfill, make the EXISTING screen measurable) is a genuine integrity win with no new alpha claim attached, and it is a prerequisite for any future test anyway. Do that; skip the theme mapper.
rejected_options: Extend the sample with another free news archive to fix the 53-month problem — rejected: I found no verified free, point-in-time, firm-linked news archive reaching back far enough (the verified one, Alpha Vantage, starts 2022-02-24). Any archive that is event-coded rather than firm-linked requires an LLM linkage step, which re-imports the memorisation problem it was meant to solve.

Prompt the LLM to ignore knowledge after the as-of date so the backtest is clean — rejected on measured evidence: 97.6% vs 98.0% accuracy with and without the instruction in the fake-2010-cutoff test (arXiv 2504.14765). The mitigation demonstrably does not work.

Use a chronologically-consistent LLM (ChronoBERT/ChronoGPT) to get an uncontaminated backtest — technically the correct answer and the only clean path, but rejected on this project's constraints: it is not free to run at scale on a single 16GB Mac, and it does not fix the 53-month sample-length problem, which is the binding constraint.

Buy a supply-chain knowledge graph (FactSet Supply Chain, Bloomberg SPLC) — the exact recommendation the closest published analog makes for scaling. Rejected: violates the STRICTLY $0 metered constraint.

Trade the fast news-drift channel where the documented alpha actually lives — rejected by operator decision, and independently by the numbers: Ke-Kelly-Xiu's net-Sharpe optimum sits at 46% DAILY turnover, which is cost-negative for this system.

Ship it as a 15th apply_*_to_score overlay routed through overlay_math.sign_safe_mult and gate it later — rejected: the backtest engine has zero news features, so the overlay would be structurally un-gate-able exactly like news_screen is today. Adding a second un-measurable overlay makes the integrity problem worse, not better.

Build the cross-sector theme map first and validate second, on the argument that the four reference cases are self-evidently real — rejected: all four are famous, heavily-written-about narratives inside every frontier model's training corpus. Confirming them is recall, not evidence, and selecting the four cases that worked is textbook narrative survivorship (metaverse, cannabis, 3D printing and clean-energy ETFs are the unselected denominator; Morningstar records >3/4 of 15-year thematic funds shuttered).

Relax the promotion gate for this signal because the data is young — rejected: gates are immutable in this project, and relaxing them here would be relaxing them for exactly the signal class with the worst documented base rate.
open_questions: WHAT WOULD CHANGE MY MIND (1): a verified FREE, point-in-time, firm-linked news or theme archive reaching back to ~2005 or earlier, giving 240+ monthly observations. At T=240 the DSR-required Sharpe at N=45 trials falls toward ~1.5, which is at least in the same universe as documented effect sizes. Does such an archive exist within the $0 constraint? I did not find one.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE MY MIND (2): evidence that a VALUE-WEIGHTED, large-cap-only, <=12%/month-turnover cross-sector news signal clears t>2.78 in a single pre-registered specification. Every value-weighted number I found is 0.67-1.33 Sharpe or t<2.78. One clean counterexample would reopen the question.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE MY MIND (3): evidence that the news effect is NOT concentrated in the 1-4 day window. Ke-Kelly-Xiu is the load-bearing citation for my horizon argument and it uses Dow Jones Newswires 2004-2017. Has anyone measured the firm-level news-return decay curve on a post-2020 sample, where retail attention and passive flows are structurally different?

WHAT WOULD CHANGE MY MIND (4): a chronologically-consistent (pre-cutoff-frozen) LLM producing the theme->beneficiary map, so that the backtest measures foresight rather than recall. He/Lv/Manela/Wu (2025) ChronoBERT/ChronoGPT is the named vehicle; is there a CPU-runnable checkpoint small enough for a 16GB M4?

UNRESOLVED: is the Cohen-Frazzini decay (VW t=1.54 in 2005-2018) evidence the mechanism is dead, or evidence it moved to a channel that requires better link data than public 10-K customer disclosures? The Customer Momentum authors attribute it to "post-publication exploitation by investors", which favours the dead reading, but I could not falsify the alternative.

UNRESOLVED: I could not read Chen and Zimmermann in full (only the abstract-level claims via search). Their 98%-replication result and 12.3% bias adjustment are the strongest rebuttal to my base-rate argument and deserve a full read before this lens is treated as settled. My scope-limitation argument (their sample is numeric CRSP/Compustat characteristics with multi-decade histories, not 4-year LLM text mappings) is reasoning, not measurement.

UNVERIFIED BY ME: the Alpha Vantage NEWS_SENTIMENT 2022-02-24 start date was given to me as a measured fact and my central computation depends on it. Worth re-confirming with a live call — though the conclusion is robust to +/- 1 year (T=53 -> T=65 moves the N=45 required Sharpe only from ~1.97 to ~1.9).

OPEN: the Ben-David media-sentiment result (-0.53%/month for high-media-sentiment launches) is measured on ETF LAUNCH timing, which involves a months-long product-development lag. Would a faster theme detector front-run that lag rather than replicate it? I have no evidence either way, and the Morningstar 4.9pp investor gap suggests even fast tactical traders lose to it.

lens: INTERNAL CODEBASE AUDIT — pyfinagent repo at /Users/ford/.openclaw/workspace/pyfinagent (read-only, no web research)
bottom_line: A cross-sector theme overlay is a ~150-line drop-in on the LIVE path (defense_signal.py is a 1-theme special case of exactly the right shape, and rank_candidates already accepts 14 keyword-arg overlays), but it is currently UNGATEABLE: the backtest engine has a completely separate, overlay-free scoring path (candidate_selector.py:175-206), _NUMERIC_FEATURES (backtest_engine.py:50-60) has no hook for a per-ticker theme score, and the "promotion gate" that would evaluate it (scripts/risk/gauntlet.py) is dry-run-stub-only by design (gauntlet.py:16-21) and evaluates only drawdown ratios — not DSR, not PBO, not beat-incumbent. The binding constraint is the evaluation harness, not the signal.

key_findings.claim: defense_signal.py is a hard-coded ONE-theme instance of exactly the shape a generic theme engine needs. Theme DETECTION = AND-gate of two cycle-level scalars: (a) `_fetch_gpr_acts(...)['above_threshold']` from macro_regime (defense_signal.py:103-115) and (b) `_fetch_xar_momentum(window)` > `xar_min_momentum`, a yfinance 5-day cumulative return on the literal ticker string "XAR" (defense_signal.py:49-80, `yf.download("XAR", ...)` at line 59). `triggered = gpr_above and xar_above` (line 133). BENEFICIARY SET = a flat CSV ticker list, no sector/graph logic: `defense_tickers_csv` default "LMT,NOC,RTX,GD,LHX,BA,LDOS,HII,KTOS,BAE.L,RHM.DE,SAAB-B.ST" (defense_signal.py:84), sourced live from `settings.defense_tickers` (settings.py:526) via autonomous_loop.py:719.
